controlsMoving.title: Controls: Moving Around
controlsMoving.description:
[Arrows] or [WASD] move. [Z] or [Enter] confirms and talks. [X] or [Esc] cancels. Hold [Shift] to run.

Running spends [AP | combatAP], the same meter your battle skills use. Stand still or walk to get it back.

[Z] acts on the tile you face. On a companion it opens a short menu: a word on the road, their [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] sheet, or the reserves.

[Tab] makes the next member the leader, [Shift] and [Tab] the previous one.

controlsMenus.title: Controls: Menu Hotkeys
controlsMenus.description:
[Esc] or [right click] opens the menu. Hold [Tab] for the quick menu. On the map each screen also has a letter key:

- [I] backpack, [C] status, [O] equipment, [U] skills, [J] quests
- [M] world map, [B] build, [V] vehicles, [R] wait and rest, [K] cooking
- [H] this book, [N] training, [P] hyperdeck, [L] politics

Inside the menu, [1] opens the [Thinker | craftThinker]. On the map, [1] to [9] use the quick bar.

[F9] quicksave, [F10] quickload, [F11] fullscreen, [F3] screenshot. If you are ever stuck, hold [Ctrl] to walk through walls while [CTRL noclip | optionsMenu] is on.

controlsMouse.title: Controls: Mouse
controlsMouse.description:
The mouse does not move your character.

- [drag] pans the camera. It snaps back when you walk
- [wheel] or [+] and [-] zoom the world map
- [hover] over something to see its name
- [right click] opens the menu

In battle: [left click] an enemy to use the selected command on it, [wheel] scrolls the commands, [1] to [9] cast the skills on the quick bar.

controlsGamepad.title: Controls: Controller
controlsGamepad.description:
A controller works on the map, in menus and in battle.

- [left stick] or [D-pad] moves, [right stick] pans the camera
- [A] confirms, [B] cancels, [X] runs, [Y] opens the menu. Hold [Y] for the quick menu
- [L1] / [R1] step the quick bar on the map and change tab in menus
- [L2] / [R2] change character in menus. On the map [R2] changes the leader and a tap of [L2] folds the map notes
- hold [L2] and push the [right stick] to zoom the world map
- [L3] vehicles, [R3] build, [Start] wait and rest

[Search fields | controlsSearch] are hidden on a controller.

controlsRemap.title: Controls: Remapping
controlsRemap.description:
Keys and buttons cannot be rebound. Keyboard and controller both work at all times.

The full lists are on [Controls: Menu Hotkeys | controlsMenus] and [Controls: Controller | controlsGamepad].

controlsScreen.title: What Is On The Screen
controlsScreen.description:
The [party HUD] sits top left: each member's name, level, [HP], [AP | combatAP] and [MP]. In battle the one acting is lit.

Small [chips] beside each card warn you of trouble: a need running low, a [craving | needsAddiction], an [illness | healthDiseases], a state. They change colour as things get worse.

In a vehicle, the vehicle gets its own row above the crew, with its condition and [fuel | vehicleFuel].

The [quick bar] sits bottom centre: items on the map, skills in battle.

controlsSearch.title: Searching Inside Menus
controlsSearch.description:
Every long list has a search strip, this book included. Click the magnifier at the top of the page, or press [F], to open it.

- while you type, menu hotkeys stay quiet
- [Escape] empties the field, [Escape] again leaves it
- on a controller the magnifier is hidden

The [main menu search] looks across several screens at once: your items, your companions' gear, skills, recipes, creatures.

savingGame.title: Saving, Autosave and Quicksaves
savingGame.description:
The game [autosaves] when you change map. How often is up to you in [Options | optionsMenu].

[F9] quicksaves and [F10] loads the latest quicksave, on the map whenever nothing else is happening. The [rest menu | needsRestWorth] has a Save entry too.

The save screen also lists the other parties of your world. You can load them, but never save over them.

You cannot save on the floors of [the dungeon | worldDungeon]. The [sandbox | setupSandbox] keeps its own save apart from everything else.

Warning: under [permadeath | partyDeath], death deletes that party's saves for good. Its [diary | societyDiary] survives.

worldsFolders.title: Worlds and Savegames
worldsFolders.description:
A [world] is a place that outlives any one adventure. A default world called [Esoteric] is always there. You can make more on the [Worlds] screen, see [Creating a World | setupWorldCreation].

Each world arrives already lived in, with [a century of history | societyHistory], people, homes, jobs and politics of its own.

Every party you play in a world shares it, and inherits what the others left behind. An emptied chest stays empty, built furniture stays built, and time only moves [forward].

Your other parties live on as [characters on the map], going about their day. You can stop and talk with them.

Warning: deleting a world deletes all of its savegames. Esoteric can only be reset, which wipes its history and saves.

optionsMenu.title: Options
optionsMenu.description:
Options is split into tabs:

- [Gameplay]: language, [difficulty | combatModes], [map battles | combatMapBattle], [fog of war | worldFog], dialogue, autosave
- [Video]: theme, fullscreen, scaling, text size
- [Audio]: volumes, battle music, voices
- [Shader]: the retro look of the 3D scenes
- [Experimental]: the [auto explorer | partyAutoIdle], ASCII mode, CTRL noclip and other curiosities

[CTRL noclip] is on by default: hold [Ctrl] to walk straight through walls and encounters. Use it to get free if you are ever stuck.

modsUpdates.title: Mods and Updates
modsUpdates.description:
The desktop game reads a [mods] folder next to it. Drop a mod in and it can change or add almost anything.

In the [Mod Manager], [Enter] turns a mod on or off and [Page Up] / [Page Down] change the load order. The mod at the [bottom] wins. Changes apply the next time you start.

The [UPDATES] entry on the title screen fetches the newest build and asks you to reopen the game. You can pick a stable or an unstable channel, and go back to an earlier build if you need to.

partyBasics.title: The Party
partyBasics.description:
The party holds [3 members]. The first is the [leader], the one you steer. [Tab] passes the lead on.

A [4th companion | partyPets] can walk along too, outside the fighting.

Each member has their own [needs | needsOverview], opinions and [specializations | progressSpecializations], and their own feelings about the other two. Left to themselves they wander near the leader, and slip off to eat, wash or rest when they need to, paid from the party purse.

Run for a moment to call everyone back in.

partyCreation.title: Making Your Characters
partyCreation.description:
You make your characters one at a time, up to [3], in one of three ways:

- [Simple]: look, class, [traits | partyTraits], gear
- [Dossiers]: ready made characters, some with a vehicle or a hometown of their own. Some can be used only once
- [Detailed]: the whole sheet, down to beliefs and backstory

Your [class | partyClasses] decides your starting kit.

partyClasses.title: Classes
partyClasses.description:
A class shapes who you start as: your stats, your kit, a [favoured element | elementsOverview] and the schools of magic and skill that come naturally to you.

Skills from your own schools are cheaper in [knowledge points | progressKnowledge]. Other schools open up once you have a foothold in them, at a steeper price.

Any class can use any weapon. How well is a [trainable proficiency | gearProficiency].

[Creature classes | partyCreatures], such as Feral, Ghost or Drone, are something else: in the world they are animals, not people.

partyTraits.title: Traits
partyTraits.description:
Traits are chosen at creation with a small budget of points. Strengths cost points, drawbacks give some back.

They shape your stats, hand you skills and gear, and colour how people and the world react to you.

Most traits are yours for life. Only [genetic] ones can change later, through [gene splicing | healthSurgery], for [100 euros] per point.

partyAttributes.title: Attributes
partyAttributes.description:
Six attributes describe a body and a mind:

- [STR]: physical attack, [carrying capacity | gearWeight]
- [CON]: physical defense, carrying capacity
- [INT]: magic attack
- [WIS]: magic defense
- [DEX]: who acts first, dodging
- [PSI]: luck. Critical hits, [rare finds | gearRarity] and fortune in general

partyCreatures.title: Playing A Creature
partyCreatures.description:
A party member can be a [creature], built from one species or two crossed together.

The species gives the body: its limbs, its reach, its hands or lack of them, and its [weak points | combatBodyParts]. Anatomy decides how many [weapons it can hold | gearSlots] and even what a [pregnancy | partyReproduction] brings.

Out in the world, a creature on a [creature class | partyClasses] is an animal. Yours keep their money and belongings all the same. Pick a [civilised class] instead and you are a person shaped like an animal.

partyPortraits.title: Portraits and 3D Models
partyPortraits.description:
Each character is shown as a hand drawn [bust] or a [3D model]. Pick one on the Bio tab and switch whenever you like.

The model is built from parts of any creature, with sliders to shape it. People default to a bust, creatures to a model.

[Recruited | partyRecruiting] monsters and [summons | combatSummons] wear their species' body. The status screen, dialogue and the [Empathize panel | peopleEmpathize] all follow your choice.

partyRecruiting.title: Recruiting People
partyRecruiting.description:
There are three ways to win someone over: [talk a monster round | combatTalk], ask a townsperson through [Empathize | peopleEmpathize], or adopt and train a creature.

The better someone thinks of you, the likelier they say yes, so build their [opinion | peopleOpinion] first. People far stronger than you will not follow.

The panel offers [Join Party], or [Join as Follower]: they walk behind you as your [4th companion | partyPets] instead.

A recruit brings their whole life with them. The party travels three strong, so anyone extra waits in the [Reserves]. A dismissed member goes home.

Even a shopkeeper can be lured from behind the counter. Some people, though, will never leave the life they have.

partyPets.title: Pets, Followers and Children
partyPets.description:
A [4th companion] can follow the party without fighting or coming to harm. The exception is a [familiar | partyFamiliar], which fights beside you.

A [follower] is a talking monster or a person who chose to come along. A [pet] is a creature that does not talk, a [child] comes from a [pregnancy | partyReproduction]. Pick who walks with you on the [Followers] page.

Warning: abandoning a pet or, far worse, a child is a [crime | lawCrime]. A follower can be sent away freely.

Given time on the road, pets and followers can be [trained] into full party members. [Animal Training | progressSpecializations] speeds it up.

Most companions can be marked [Ridable] and [ridden | partyRiding], and the [Summon Beast | combatSummons] rite calls your pet into a fight.

partyReproduction.title: Reproduction and Pregnancy
partyReproduction.description:
Every body has its own way of making new life, set by its species. Some carry children, some lay eggs, some grow seeds, and some simply split in two.

A pregnancy runs its course, and [Biologics | bodyBiologics] lets you follow it. Expect symptoms along the way.

Newborns and hatchlings appear in [Followers | partyPets] as children who take after their parent.

partyDeath.title: Death, Gravestones and Permadeath
partyDeath.description:
A killing blow on a healthy member usually leaves them hanging on. You can always flee, except from a boss.

A fallen member normally just loses consciousness and comes round later. If the whole party goes down, you wake up healed: at your [last save | savingGame] on a hand made map, or out in the open world where you last [slept in camp | needsCamp].

Warning: under [Permadeath | combatModes] or [Blood and Oil], allies not revived before the battle ends are gone for good, and the others grieve them. A full wipe leaves a [gravestone] and deletes the party's saves. The world goes on.

Healing does not regrow [severed limbs | bodyParts].

partyBanterPage.title: What Your Companions Say
partyBanterPage.description:
Your companions talk among themselves about whatever is going on: something you just bought, a wound, the weather, the money, the leader's latest plan, something from the [diary | societyDiary].

Each one's [personality] colours what they say, and they keep chatting on the road, in the car and on the train.

partyAutoIdle.title: The Auto Explorer
partyAutoIdle.description:
An [Experimental | optionsMenu] option lets the game play for you while you stand still. Touch anything and control comes straight back. An AUTO badge shows while it plays.

It wanders from map to map, eats, heals, shops, learns skills, [works the land | worldTerrain] and fights, keeping clear of fights it cannot win and of the police when you are [wanted | lawCrime].

The leader's [morality] shows in how it plays. A kind leader chats with people. A ruthless one may [steal | econStealing] what the party needs, and take the consequences.

progressLevels.title: Levels and Experience
progressLevels.description:
Experience comes mostly from [winning fights], and also from [adventures | worldAdventures] and [research | worldTechTree]. Each level makes you a little stronger all round.

Levels are only part of your power. Skills, [specializations | progressSpecializations], gear and your body matter more.

progressKnowledge.title: Knowledge Points
progressKnowledge.description:
[Knowledge points], or KP, are what you spend to learn and create skills. They belong to the whole party, and the total is shown in the [Training | progressTraining] menu. Every new member brings a gift of KP the first time they join.

You earn KP by being curious:

- winning fights, especially against stronger foes
- [quests | econQuests], [adventures | worldAdventures] and [anomalies | galaxyAnomalies]
- [dreams | worldDreams] and [foraging | needsForage]
- reading a [book | pastimesReading] or studying a statue or fossil for the first time
- [Raman scans | gamesRaman] and new pages in the [browser | hypernetBrowser]
- [Hexorcizing | progressHexorcize] magical gear

You spend it on:

- skills on the [school trees | progressAtlas]
- [fusing spells | progressFusion], [writing your own | progressWorkbench], [enchanting | progressEnchanting] and [writing books | progressWritingBooks]
- [Introspect] in the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel, to change who you are

Your own schools cost less. Learning from a person in Empathize costs euros instead, and a friend teaches for free.

progressAtlas.title: The Skill Atlas
progressAtlas.description:
Each school is a hand drawn [tree]. The roots sit at the top and every row below grows stronger.

To buy a skill you must know the ones it grows from. In your own schools the roots are always open. The deepest [Esoteric] and [Forbidden] branches also wait until you are experienced enough. A [Cultist | partyClasses] learns nothing here, only from [books | progressGrimoires].

Use the arrows by the school's name to change tree. [Wheel] or [+] and [-] zoom, [drag] pans.

progressTraining.title: Training and Progression
progressTraining.description:
Skills are bought with [KP | progressKnowledge] in the [Training] menu, instantly.

The more you use a skill, the better you get at its school, through [specializations | progressSpecializations]. Practice makes it hit harder and heal more.

progressSpecializations.title: Specializations
progressSpecializations.description:
Specializations are everything you can get good at, from Wrestling to Accounting to Beekeeping. Each climbs from Untrained to Master.

You learn by doing. Cooking makes you a better cook, haggling a sharper trader, casting a stronger caster. Whoever does the work learns the most, and the rest of the party picks up a little. [Minigames | gamesOverview] teach too.

Your [class | partyClasses] and [traits | partyTraits] can give you a head start. Points left over at [character creation | partyCreation] are [banked]: spend them in the Specializations menu to jump a specialization up a tier.

They matter everywhere: forging, [lockpicking | gamesLockpick], [wrestling holds | combatWrestle], shop prices, quest pay, even whether you can read a recipe.

progressPassives.title: Class Passives
progressPassives.description:
Every [class | partyClasses] has one [signature passive] that is always working for you, in battle and out. Some [traits | partyTraits] add their own. Only the three party members count.

Find them on the status sheet under [Class Abilities].

progressLoadout.title: The Nine Skill Slots
progressLoadout.description:
Each character carries [9 skills] into a fight, filling the [battle quick bar]. Basic moves and skills lent by gear come free.

Some skills ask for a minimum in a [stat | partyAttributes], and only your own body and training count, not your gear. If you fall short you cannot carry the skill.

A skill lent by gear can be used anyway, but it may [fumble], wasting its [MP | combatAP]. The skill card warns you how risky it is.

Change your loadout between fights as often as you like.

progressFusion.title: Fusing Spells
progressFusion.description:
[Fuse Spells], on the right page of [Training | progressTraining], melts two abilities a member knows into something new.

1. Pick the member in the companion tabs.
2. Put a spell in the [dominant] slot. It sets the shape of the result.
3. Put a spell or skill in the [recessive] slot.
4. Pick an animation, or keep the old one.
5. Press create and roll.

The new ability carries the effects of both, costs both, and can be renamed. It costs [KP | progressKnowledge], and your [INT | partyAttributes] helps the [roll | partyDiceChecks]. A perfect roll creates something exceptional.

Warning: on a failure the KP is lost and both parts are forgotten. You can buy them again on the [tree | progressAtlas].

You cannot fuse an already fused or [crafted | progressWorkbench] ability. Later, [Split] gives you the two parts back, and [Dissolve] trades the ability for some of its KP.

progressGrimoires.title: Grimoires and Skill Books
progressGrimoires.description:
A [grimoire] opens to a handful of workings, and one reader may take one. The offers are fixed once the book is opened: closing it or changing reader will not change them.

A reader can only take a working they are ready for, with enough MP and the right [stats | progressLoadout]. Forbidden pages ask for more.

Luck, your party's [PSI | partyAttributes], makes darker pages more likely. Beyond the school grimoires and skill books lies the [Forbidden Grimoire], which offers nothing else.

progressBladeSeeds.title: Blade Seeds
progressBladeSeeds.description:
A [Blade Seed] is a spirit weapon bound to the founder of your party. Choose one seed weapon, one for each kind of weapon.

Its spirit grows with the founder's [experience | progressLevels] and evolves as it does. Its gifts only work while the weapon is in hand, and every ordinary strike teaches the spirit something new.

gearSlots.title: Equipment: Hands and Slots
gearSlots.description:
What you can hold depends on your [body | bodyParts]. A hand takes a weapon or a shield, a [two handed] weapon needs both, and a creature with no hands can still bite down on a blade.

Wielding more than one weapon is clumsy unless your [class | partyClasses] knows Dual Wield.

Warning: in [Blood and Oil | combatModes], losing a limb drops whatever it held.

gearProficiency.title: Weapon Proficiency
gearProficiency.description:
Any class can pick up any weapon, but skill with each kind is a [specialization | progressSpecializations] of its own. Your [class | partyClasses] already knows its traditional weapons. The rest start clumsy.

An untrained hand gets far less out of a weapon, a master gets more. Every battle you win with a weapon equipped teaches you a little.

gearScaling.title: What a Weapon Scales On
gearScaling.description:
Each weapon draws its strength from one or two stats. Most rely on [STR | partyAttributes], firearms on [DEX], the heaviest on both.

The equip screen highlights which stats a weapon uses.

gearArmor.title: Armour and Derived Stats
gearArmor.description:
What you wear says something about you. Your outfit gives you four looks: [Arcane], [Substance], [Stealth] and [Intimidation].

- robes and staves look arcane
- daggers, bows and light armour look stealthy
- heavy armour, axes and guns look intimidating

People notice. Your look sways how they feel in [Empathize | peopleEmpathize], and how [theft | econStealing], bribes, romance and [recruiting | partyRecruiting] go.

gearModifiers.title: Modifiers on Gear
gearModifiers.description:
A weapon or piece of armour can carry a [modifier] that changes its character and its price.

A few you may meet on weapons:
- [Sharp] cuts deeper, [Venomous] [poisons | poison], [Chilling] can [freeze | freeze]
- [Vampiric] drinks life back, [Berserk] hits terribly hard but leaves you exposed
- [Dull] and [Broken] are worth less

And on armour:
- [Regenerative] heals you, [Retaliating] adds [counterattacks | counterAttack]
- [Blessed] softens blows, [Worn] is cheaper and weaker

Look for them on the custom pieces people carry.

gearWeight.title: Weight and Encumbrance
gearWeight.description:
Only what sits in the [backpack | gearBackpack] weighs anything. What you wear is free, and food is light.

The whole party shares one load, and strong, sturdy members carry more of it ([STR | partyAttributes] and CON). The weight readout turns orange as you near the limit. Go over and you slow to a crawl until you drop something.

A [vehicle | vehiclesOverview] carries everything without complaint.

gearBackpack.title: The Backpack
gearBackpack.description:
The backpack is sorted into tabs, with the [weight readout | gearWeight], a detail card and a favourites bar.

[9 favourite slots] hold usable items and share the quick bar with your [battle skills | progressLoadout].

- on the map, [1] to [9] use the item in that slot
- in the backpack, the same keys put the item you are looking at into a slot
- [drag] an item onto a slot, [right click] to clear it

gearArtifacts.title: Artifacts
gearArtifacts.description: No artifacts turn up for now. The closest thing: some people carry a [unique piece] made just for them, and its description remembers every hand it has passed through.

gearContainers.title: Containers and Storage
gearContainers.description:
Chests, cupboards, crates and sacks hold as much as you like. Emptying one in somebody's home is [theft | lawCrime].

An [extradimensional container | craftContainers] and the holds of your [vehicles | vehiclesOverview] travel with you.

gearRarity.title: Loot and Rarity
gearRarity.description:
[Random loot | craftLoot] grows with the whole party's strength. Dangerous ground and the [Omega Tower | omegaTower] pay best.

Items wear their [rarity colour] in the backpack and in shops, and every item has its own [lore], the same each time you meet it in a world.

needsOverview.title: The Six Needs
needsOverview.description:
Every party member has six needs: [Hunger | needsHunger], [Sleep | needsSleep], [Hygiene | needsHygiene], [Company | needsSocial], [Fun | needsLeisure] and [Bladder | needsBladder]. They drain as time passes, and time passes as you walk. Running makes them drain faster.

Company is different: travelling together keeps it up, and only a lone traveller grows lonely.

A chip appears beside a member's card when a need runs low. Do not ignore it: an empty stomach starts to hurt, and a tired body recovers poorly.

Some [augments | healthAugments] can slow a need, or silence it altogether.

needsHunger.title: Hunger and Nutrition
needsHunger.description:
Everything you eat has [calories], fat and protein. A meal is worth what it contains, not what it costs.

You can eat past full, but an overstuffed stomach empties faster and gorging too far brings [Nausea | nausea].

Bitter cold and heavy heat both make you hungry sooner.

Let hunger run dry and the whole party starts losing health with every step until somebody eats.

needsSleep.title: Sleep, Rest and Time Awake
needsSleep.description:
Two things wear on you: how tired you are, and how long you have gone without real sleep.

The [sleep meter] dips as you travel. Coffee or a seat tops it up, and a tired party recovers less MP on the road.

[Time awake] only resets in a real bed or a cryogenic pod. Go days without it and [dreams | worldDreams] turn hostile and the party's mind starts to fray.

Beds, campfires, tents and world map [camps | needsCamp] open the [rest menu | needsRestWorth]. [Wait], from the menu or the [R] key, passes time and lets you sleep rough where you stand, though it is a poor night unless you carry bedding.

[Cryogenic sleep] lets you skip ahead to a day you choose, for [30 euros] a day. The world moves on without you, and you wake exactly as you went in, wounds and all.

needsHygiene.title: Hygiene, and What It Costs You
needsHygiene.description:
Hygiene fades slowly. Wash at a washroom, shower, sink or fountain. Companions left to wander will find one themselves.

People notice. A grubby traveller makes a worse impression, and a grubby stranger makes a worse one on you.

How much it matters depends on [traits | partyTraits]. A Feral or Ascetic soul hardly cares, while the Proud, the Noble and the Germaphobe care a great deal.

When [courting], a bath can make all the difference.

needsSocial.title: Company
needsSocial.description:
Company fills on its own while you travel with someone, and a [pet | partyPets] helps too. Only a lone traveller feels it drain.

[Talking | peopleEmpathize] also helps, to townspeople or among your own. A companion left loose and short of company will strike up a conversation by themselves.

Winning someone's [regard | peopleOpinion] warms the whole party. Losing it stings a little.

needsLeisure.title: Fun
needsLeisure.description:
Fun slowly drains as you walk. Refill it by [playing | gamesOverview]: arcade cabinets, pool, bowling, cards, books, TV, the [arena | combatArena].

A game won lifts spirits a lot, a game lost brings them down. Games of chance can also feed a [gambling craving | needsAddiction].

A won fight cheers the party, especially those who love a scrap. A Pacifist takes no joy in it.

Losing a companion for good hurts, more so for those who were close. A joke or a story that lands in conversation brightens everyone, and an Entertainer in the party keeps spirits up.

needsAddiction.title: Cravings and Withdrawal
needsAddiction.description:
Some [traits] are dependencies: alcohol, caffeine, nicotine, narcotics, gambling. Only a member who has one feels the craving.

The meter runs backwards: empty is content, full is [withdrawal | withdrawal]. Feed the habit and it settles. One dose rarely clears withdrawal on its own.

Cravings ease while you sleep.

bodyParts.title: Limbs and Organs
bodyParts.description:
Every character and monster is made of [limbs and organs], each able to be hurt on its own.

Most blows land on one part. [Area | combatDamageTypes] and explosive damage spread across several.

A part at zero is [broken] and holds you back until it heals. Lose a hand and you lose the weapon it held. Hurt legs slow you down.

[Vital organs | combatBodyParts] can be struck by any blow, but a monster holds on until it is badly weakened.

Healing items, spells and a night in a bed mend parts. A [clinic | healthSurgery] can repair or replace them.

In [Blood and Oil | combatModes] damage is permanent: a blade can take a limb off, [augment | healthAugments] and all.

Open the status sheet and look under [Anatomy] to see your body part by part.

bodyBiologics.title: Biologics
bodyBiologics.description:
[Biologics] is a close look at what goes on inside you: vital signs, hormones, the immune system, the brain, the [Ley Veins] and any [diseases | healthDiseases] you carry.

Your heart and hormones answer to hunger, sleep, what ails you and even [pregnancy | partyReproduction]. A badly [hurt limb | bodyParts] can choke the vein that runs through it.

healthDiseases.title: Diseases
healthDiseases.description:
Illness spreads by many roads: the air, a bite, a touch, a kiss and worse. Your own members can pass it among themselves, and you can catch it from the people you [meet | peopleEmpathize].

A new illness stays nameless for a few days. Until then, nobody can say what it is.

Healing potions do nothing against disease. You need [medicine], taken day after day. Once an illness has a name, a sick member takes the right medicine from the backpack each morning by themselves. Skip too many days and the cure starts over. Left untreated, an illness can turn into something worse.

Illness wears you down but never kills. Beat one and you may be immune, though some always find their way back.

A doctor's [Diagnose] names what you carry, for [25 euros] each. A [Nurse | partyClasses] in the party names them all for free.

healthEpidemics.title: Epidemics
healthEpidemics.description:
Beyond single illnesses, whole [epidemics] roll across the continent, town by town, until people rally and the wave breaks.

An [outbreak] is a true pathogen. A [hysteria] is a mass panic, far less deadly but strange: dancing fevers, phantom gassers and worse. You catch a hysteria by witnessing it and spread it by talking about it.

An infected town changes: moods sour, shops empty, gossip and the [news | societyNews] fill with it. Follow it all from the [Eurodemics | hypernetEurodemics] observatory.

healthSurgery.title: Clinics, Prosthetics and Field Surgery
healthSurgery.description:
A [clinic] can fit, remove, replace or [repair] a body part, or graft an [implant | healthAugments]. The price depends on the part and what it gives you. A clinic never fails. Vital parts cannot be removed.

Repair restores a damaged part still attached, and can even save one ruined in [Blood and Oil | combatModes]. A part that came off cannot be repaired: fit a new one.

The clinic also offers [plastic surgery | partyMetamorphosis] for a new body ([100 euros]) and face surgery for a new portrait ([50 euros]).

[Field surgery] is the same work on the road, for free. Pick a patient and a surgeon and use only parts you carry. It is a gamble: the odds are shown first, and a skilled [surgeon | progressSpecializations], a roof and good weather all help. A botched operation wounds the patient elsewhere.

healthAugments.title: Augments
healthAugments.description:
The [Augments] register shows what the party wears under [Fitted], and everything that exists under [Catalogue], so you can read before you pay for the graft.

A body can only take so many augments. A tougher [constitution | partyAttributes] makes room for more.

The right augment can also slow, stop or even reverse a [need | needsOverview].

healthWeatherBody.title: Weather, Temperature and the Body
healthWeatherBody.description:
The travel card shows the [temperature]. Cold and heat both make you [hungry sooner | needsHunger].

Bad [weather | worldWeather] also makes [field surgery | healthSurgery] riskier.

combatBasics.title: How a Fight Starts
combatBasics.description:
There are [no random encounters]. Every monster stands on the map with its [level | combatEnemyLevels] over its head. Walk into it to fight.

Monsters nearby may [join the fight]. Something far above your level fights alone.

Each battler acts on its own turn, and [agility | partyAttributes] decides who goes first.

A monster you ran from stays wounded while you remain on the map. Leave, and the monsters heal and the [corpses | combatCorpses] are gone.

[Fleeing] always works, except against a [boss], where it may take a few tries.

combatCommands.title: The Battle Commands
combatCommands.description:
The command menu has [Attack], [Skills], [Defense], [Backpack | gearBackpack], [Actions], [Talk | combatTalk] and [Run | combatBasics]. All skills, magic included, sit under Skills.

Defense changes with what you hold:
- a ranged weapon turns it into [Reload | combatAmmo]
- gear with a bound special skill shows that skill
- a character pushed to the brink sees their [Hyper | combatHyper]

[Actions] opens a second page:
- [Aim | combatBodyParts]: pick a part of the enemy for your next blow
- [Throw | combatThrow]: hurl an item from the pack
- [Wrestle | combatWrestle]: grab hold of the enemy

Wrestle and Talk come from the body, not the class, and never take a [loadout | progressLoadout] slot. A creature without language cannot Talk.

Mouse: [left click] an enemy to target it, [right click] to go back. Keys [1] to [9] use the quick bar: hold to arm a slot, release to cast.

combatAP.title: MP and AP
combatAP.description:
[MP] is magic. Spells spend it, and some [summons | combatSummons] feed on it.

[AP] is momentum. Battle skills and sprinting on the map draw from the same meter. Running drains it, walking slowly refills it, and standing still refills it faster.

The name tells you the cost: [magic | camelcaseMagic] is written in CamelCase and costs MP. A plain worded [skill] usually costs AP.

combatBodyParts.title: Hitting What You Aim At
combatBodyParts.description:
Monsters have limbs and organs just like you. [Aim | combatCommands] picks one for your next blow and shows your chance to hit it.

Big parts are easier to hit, small ones harder, and a part already hurt is easier still.

[Vital organs | bodyParts] are hard to hit and only finish a monster once it is badly weakened. [Blunt | combatDamageTypes] blows never finish one.

Break a limb and you take away what it does. A final cutting, piercing or explosive blow can [sever] it.

combatDamageTypes.title: Damage Types & Piercing Mechanics
combatDamageTypes.description:
Every attack has a [damage type]: Explosive, Piercing, Cutting, Blunt, Area and a few stranger ones.

Cutting, piercing and explosive blows can take a part off. Area and explosive damage spread across the body.

[Blunt] blows break bones but never destroy a [vital organ | bodyParts]. Someone beaten down with blunt blows is left [downed | lawDowned] rather than dead.

[Piercing] slips past most defences, even [Divine Shield | divineShield] and [Magic Reflection | magicReflection].

combatWrestle.title: Wrestling
combatWrestle.description:
Anyone with a [limb | bodyParts] able to grip can [Wrestle]. It costs nothing and needs no training.

You choose which of your limbs takes hold, which of theirs, and how. Each choice shows its odds.

A few of the holds:
- [Grapple]: take hold. Most other moves need one first
- [Strike]: a blow that can [concuss | concussed] or cause [bleeding | bleeding]
- [Joint lock]: [pins | pinned] the enemy in place
- [Choke]: leaves them gasping for air
- [Rip]: a long shot that can tear the limb clean off

The [Wrestling | progressSpecializations] specialization makes you better at all of it, and a [martial art | gearMartialArts] brings finishers of its own.

combatTalk.title: Talking to Monsters
combatTalk.description:
A monster that understands you can be talked to. [Talk] opens a panel with each approach and its odds.

Every enemy has a [disposition] toward you. Hurting it sours the mood. Your [PSI | partyAttributes] and [how you look | gearArmor] help.

- [Chat]: builds rapport
- [Surrender]: asks it to leave the fight
- [Join the party | partyRecruiting]: needs a free slot and a creature of your size
- [Follow you | partyPets]: takes it along as a pet
- [Insult] and [Throw a stone]: always land, and it will like you less
- [Pet it]: a talking creature has to like you first

Some creatures are forces rather than people, [petrodemons | petrodemons] above all, and will hear none of it.

combatEnemyLevels.title: Enemy Levels and Where They Live
combatEnemyLevels.description:
How dangerous the land is depends on where you stand. Some nations are gentle places to start, others are not, and away from Europe the wild tends to match your party.

No creature belongs to one country alone. Each nation simply favours some over others.

Time matters too. The further the years run, the fiercer the world becomes.

Each world also hides a few [rarities]: creatures that exist only once, marked by a [gold] level tag and unusual colours. Meet one and it goes into the [Bestiary | combatBestiary], never to appear again.

combatMovementAI.title: How Monsters Behave
combatMovementAI.description:
Every roaming monster has its own [temperament]: how it idles, how it spots you and what it does next.

A grazer bolts when you come close. A sentry watches one direction and can be crept around. An ambusher waits until you are near, then strikes. A lone pack animal keeps its distance and calls the others. There are many more.

Monsters also live among themselves. Hunters chase prey across the map, and the prey runs.

combatSafety.title: Danger Warnings and Surviving a Blow
combatSafety.description:
A monster's level tag warns you: white is a fair fight, [yellow] is tough, [red] is deadly.

In each fight, a character at full health survives one blow that would have killed them. Someone already hurt gets no such luck.

Now and then a monster that can [talk | combatTalk] may simply [spare you] and walk away, if it likes you, if you are on your last legs, or if you are beneath its notice.

combatModes.title: Difficulty and Combat Modes
combatModes.description:
Two choices made at [character creation | partyCreation] shape every fight.

The [difficulty]:
- [Peaceful]: monsters only fight back once hurt, and nobody truly dies
- [Roguelite]: defeat wakes you at a respawn point, and fallen allies can be revived
- [Permadeath | partyDeath] and [Blood and Oil]: death is the end, and allies not revived in time are lost for good. Blood and Oil also lets blades take limbs off forever

The [battle style]:
- [Turn Battle]: the classic battle screen
- [Strategic Battle | combatMapBattle]: fights on the live map. You can change this later in [Options | optionsMenu]

combatMapBattle.title: Map Battle Mode
combatMapBattle.description:
[Strategic Battle] fights every battle right on the map where you stand. Choose it at [character creation | partyCreation] or later in [Options | optionsMenu], under Gameplay.

Everyone fights from where they are. Nearby monsters join in, and townspeople who like you, or are simply brave, may take your side.

[Move] repositions the acting battler. Water slows you. Spears and whips reach further than swords, bows and guns further still, and ranged attacks need a clear line of sight.

You [cannot run | combatBasics] with a monster right beside you. Step away first.

combatSummons.title: Summons
combatSummons.description:
A [summon] is a temporary extra member of the party. Only one can be out at a time, you command it on its turn, and when it dies it is gone.

Summoning is [Convokation] magic. Each rite calls a family of beings: demons, elementals, dragons and many stranger things. What answers is always a match for the fight at hand.

Some rites call what you prepared: a creature or a person you marked, the last thing you killed, even a companion you lost.

A summon must be paid for every turn it stays, in blood, MP, euros or stranger coin. When you cannot pay, it leaves. [DismissSummon] sends it away.

Outside a fight, what you call walks behind you for a while and joins any battle on the way. Send it home from the [Followers] page.

A [familiar] is something else: see [Familiars | partyFamiliar].

combatArena.title: The Arena
combatArena.description:
The arena offers a [gauntlet] of fights at a level you pick, a [biome trial] against one land's beasts, and a [boss rush].

Your party is brought to the bracket's level, or you can field a random roster instead.

Each win grows your [streak], and the prizes grow with it. Later fights pit you against whole groups. [Running | combatBasics] from any fight ends the streak.

combatBulletHell.title: Bullet Hell Sequences
combatBulletHell.description:
Some fights break into a [bullet hell]: you steer a small craft, weave through the enemy's fire and shoot back.

Every hit there counts in the fight.

combatSpirits.title: Spirit Battlers
combatSpirits.description:
Fallen enemies do not linger as spirits for you to field later.

To fight beside a monster, [talk it into joining | combatTalk] or call one with a [summon | combatSummons].

combatMimic.title: Mimicry
combatMimic.description:
[Mimic skills] let you borrow other bodies. Steal an enemy's skills, wear its face, turn its own last trick back on it, or become it entirely. You can even copy a companion.

Copies fade when the battle ends. [Mutation] is the exception: it fuses strange creatures into your body for good.

Taking a body means taking its [limbs | bodyParts], which changes what you can hold and where you can be hurt.

A [Mimic | partyClasses] by class picks up new tricks as they grow, and sometimes keeps a skill an enemy used on them.

combatThrow.title: Throwing Things
combatThrow.description:
You can throw items, weapons and armour. Light things fly far, heavy ones drop short.

What you throw stays where it lands, ready to be picked up, unless it falls somewhere that destroys it.

combatCorpses.title: Corpses and Rewards
combatCorpses.description:
After a win, the [reward popup] shows everything you earned: items in their [rarity | gearRarity] colours, money, experience and [knowledge | progressKnowledge].

The dead leave [corpses] on the map until you leave. A monster you beat is gone for good. One you fled from waits where it was, still wounded.

A [boss] dies once for the whole world, in every savegame of it. The kill goes into the [Historical Archive | societyHistory].

A [petrodemon | petrodemons] pays in crude oil.

Winning lifts the spirits of everyone who fought, and every creature you face goes into the [Bestiary].

elementsOverview.title: Elements: How They Work
elementsOverview.description:
Nine elements run through every fight: [Physical | elementPhysical], [Fire | elementFire], [Ice | elementIce], [Thunder | elementThunder], [Water | elementWater], [Petro | petro], [Wind | elementWind], [Sacred | elementSacred] and [Cursed | elementCursed].

Every creature has its weaknesses and resistances. Some are immune, and a few even heal from what should hurt them.

The battle HUD shows the main weaknesses of the enemy in front of you, and the [Bestiary] tells the whole story.

States change things: a [Wet | wet] target fears thunder more than fire, and an [Oily | oily] one is waiting for a spark.

elementPhysical.title: Element: Physical
elementPhysical.description:
Edges, points, weight and fists. Most weapon attacks are physical.

Physical skills can [break guards | guardBroken], [pin | pinned] or [unbalance | unbalanced] a foe. Whether a blow can sever depends on its [damage type | combatDamageTypes].

[Armour | gearArmor] stops it. Heavy armour protects more and looks fearsome, light armour helps you stay unseen.

Ghosts and most oozes shrug it off.

elementFire.title: Element: Fire
elementFire.description:
Fire often leaves a target [Burned | burned], and a burn does not go out on its own.

[Oily | oily] and [Cold | cold] targets go up fast, and plants fear it. [Wet | wet] targets and most reptiles shrug much of it off. Fire elementals and phoenixes drink it in.

elementIce.title: Element: Ice
elementIce.description:
Ice leaves a target [Cold | cold], or [Frozen | freeze] solid and unable to act.

A cold target burns all the better, so ice sets up [fire | elementFire].

elementThunder.title: Element: Thunder
elementThunder.description:
Thunder leaves a target [Static | static], or [Paralysed | paralysis] and unable to act.

[Wet | wet] and [Floating | floating] targets suffer most. One already static holds up better.

Machines, drones and armoured knights usually dread it.

elementWater.title: Element: Water
elementWater.description: Water leaves the target [Wet | wet]: weak to [thunder | elementThunder], safe from [fire | elementFire]. On its own it hits softly.

petro.title: Element: Petro
petro.description:
Oil, and whatever comes out of the ground with it.

Petro is the element of the [petrodemons | petrodemons]. They will not be reasoned with, cannot be hurt by Petro and fear [fire | elementFire]. They leave oil behind.

Oil matters beyond battle too: it prices [post | societyMail], feeds the [petrodemon summon | combatSummons] and trades on the [stock market | econStocks].

Some Petro attacks leave the target [Oily | oily], waiting for a spark.

elementWind.title: Element: Wind
elementWind.description:
Air, pressure and moving force. Wind often lifts the target into [Floating | floating], and now and then leaves it [unbalanced | unbalanced].

Most birds ride it out with ease.

elementSacred.title: Element: Sacred
elementSacred.description:
The bane of demons and the undead: skeletons, ghosts and vampires all fear it. Angels tend to resist it, and some sacred beings drink it in.

Sacred workings may [Silence | silence] or [Blind | blind] the target, and some leave a [Death Mark | deathMark].

elementCursed.title: Element: Cursed
elementCursed.description:
Rot, ruin and draining. The undead wield it more than anything else, and some cursed workings steal HP or MP from their target.

Many humans and goblins are weak to it. Robots and angels hold firm.

worldMapPage.title: The World Map
worldMapPage.description:
The world map is all of Europe, each square a whole region. Crossing one takes time, less in a vehicle.

[M] opens and closes the fullscreen map. There, [drag] to pan and use the [wheel] or [Q] / [E] to zoom. The corner minimap can be switched in the travel options.

Hover or pick a square to learn about it. [Show map] lets you look at a square before you go, and you can leave a [note] on it, also with [right click] or [R1]. Aboard a vehicle, click a named place to set off for it.

Press the [action button] for the travel menu:
- [Visit] the square you stand on
- [Investigate] an adventure
- [Liminal walk] it on foot in the [3D world | worldVoxelWalk]
- [forage], or [make a camp | needsCamp]

[T] returns to the last local map, or enters the square you stand on.

Many great cities, London, Paris, Rome and others, are [trapped in a spacetime bubble]. You cannot enter them. Squares marked [???] hold [adventures | worldAdventures].

worldProcedural.title: Procedural Maps
worldProcedural.description:
Almost every place you visit is [generated] from your world. Return to a square and you find it just as you left it.

The [biome | worldBiomes] decides how the land looks and what grows there. Roads wander and cross, rivers and coastlines run on into the next square, and handmade corners and [terrain features | worldTerrain] are scattered along the way.

Walk off the edge to step into the [neighbouring square].

worldBiomes.title: Biomes
worldBiomes.description:
The [biome] of a square shapes everything about it: the land, the creatures, the music, the [weather | worldWeather] and what you can [forage | needsForage].

Some biomes are rare and strange, like spirit woods and crystal fields, and certain creatures live nowhere else.

Roofed places, cellars, temples, caves and dungeons, are reached through a [structure entrance | worldStructures].

worldStructures.title: Structures Under the Map
worldStructures.description:
Entrances on the map are [walked into], not pressed. Each one always leads to the same place.

- [stairs down]: cellars, crypts, mines, forgotten libraries and much more. Very rarely, a [Holy Patron Bunker | galaxyPatrons]
- [stairs up]: things once built above ground and since buried
- [cave]: dens, frozen caves, crystal grottoes and stranger hollows
- [grate]: a town's sewers
- [hatch]: found only on a patron's square, where retired companions live

The land above hints at what lies below: ice hides frozen caves, a graveyard hides catacombs.

worldHouses.title: Houses, Inns and Shops
worldHouses.description:
[Doors] open onto real buildings: houses, inns, [shops | econShops] and tower blocks, some with several floors. A door always opens onto the same place.

Only [homes] lock, and only at night. Shops never do. A locked door can be [picked | gamesLockpick], and a door you force stays open for a while.

worldTerrain.title: Working the Terrain
worldTerrain.description:
Face a terrain feature and press the action button to work it.

- [trees]: felled with an [axe] in your pack
- [rocks]: mined with a [war pick], a heavy weapon or a [chipped pickaxe]
- [plants]: picked by hand
- almost anything else can be [dismantled]

You gain [crafting materials], and mining now and then turns up an [ingot].

Foraging always yields plant matter, and often something to eat. The land decides what: chanterelles in a forest, cloudberries on the tundra, dates in the desert, glowcaps underground. Training [Foraging | progressSpecializations] helps.

[Alien | galaxyLanding] worlds offer nothing to forage, but their tentacle growths can be cut for meat.

What you fell or work [stays gone].

worldDungeon.title: The Dungeon and the Tower
worldDungeon.description:
One great dungeon rises in every world, its shape different each time.

Above ground the [tower] climbs floor after floor. Every so often you reach an [elevator hall], and from there the elevator and the floor list take you back to any floor you have already reached. Floors you have not seen show as [???].

Below ground lies the [lower tower], a long descent through buried [structures | worldStructures]. Down there the numbers run the other way.

worldPuzzles.title: Puzzles
worldPuzzles.description:
Many maps hide puzzles waiting to be solved:

- [blocks] to push into place, with shrines to undo or reset
- [pressure plates], levers and gates that open only in the right combination
- [ice floors], arrows and conveyors that carry you along
- [crystal switches] that turn walls solid or open
- [torches] to light, sometimes against the clock

And stranger things still: warp pads, [crackable walls | worldDigging], beams of light, clones that copy your moves.

worldFog.title: Fog of War
worldFog.description:
[Fog of war] is an option, [off] at the start. Turn it on in the gameplay tab of [Options | optionsMenu].

With it on, the map is hidden until you explore it. You see in the direction you face, so turning is how you look around, and walls and doors block your sight. Ground you have uncovered is remembered.

In some buildings you only ever see the room you are in, and while you [dive | worldMovement] the dry land goes dark.

worldDigging.title: Digging and Secret Doors
worldDigging.description:
Some walls are [cracked]. Hold the right tool, interact, and a dead end becomes a way through. In the 3D world the [pick | worldVoxelDigging] digs through the ground itself.

[Secret doors] look like plain wall until you touch them.

A locked door offers two ways in:
- [Lockpick | gamesLockpick]: a quiet puzzle that needs [lockpicks]
- [Bash]: a test of strength

A [skeleton key] opens it outright. Breaking in counts as a [crime | lawCrime].

Some doors let you [peek] at the room beyond before you decide.

worldMovement.title: Water, Climbing and Bridges
worldMovement.description:
Face water and press the action button for the [water menu]:
- [swim]
- [fish | gamesFishing] with a rod
- [surf | gamesSurfing] with a surfboard
- [dive] with a diving suit
- [drink]
- take a [boat | vehicleBoat]

Swimming leaves the whole party cleaner, a fine way to keep up [hygiene | needsHygiene]. Swim too long and you run out of breath, especially on an empty stomach ([hunger | needsHunger]). The [Swimming | progressSpecializations] specialization lets you go further.

Fresh water eases hunger. Sea water is [salt]: drinking it leaves everyone sick with [Nausea | nausea].

On the open sea, [dive] takes you down to the seabed and [resurface] brings you back.

[Climbable] terrain asks before you climb. [Seats] and benches can be sat on, and in a place that serves food you can [order food] from your table. Hold a direction to stand up.

[Bridges] can be crossed over or passed under, depending on how you approach them.

worldWeather.title: Weather, Time and Seasons
worldWeather.description:
The clock starts on your world's [starting date | setupStartDate], 1 January 2001 by default. Time only moves when something happens: it creeps forward as you walk, stops when you stand still, and leaps ahead when you sleep, wait, [forage | needsForage], work or travel.

[Weather] follows the season, the hour and the country you are in. Cold brings snow, and rain sometimes turns into storms. Crossing into another country on the [world map | worldMapPage] can bring a change of sky.

The screen tints with the time of day and the [temperature | healthWeatherBody]: blue in the cold, red in the heat.

worldDreams.title: Dreams
worldDreams.description:
A long sleep can carry you into a [dream]. No two are alike: places you half remember, places nobody should, stitched together in ways that do not quite make sense.

- [WASD] walks, the [mouse] looks, [space] jumps. [Double tap] jump while standing to [take off]. Hold it to climb, [Ctrl] to sink
- the [action button] uses the weapon in your right hand. The [wheel] steps through others
- touching anything alive moves you to [another dream]
- holes have [no floor], and falling far enough wakes you

Every dream keeps [laws] of its own. Learn them quickly.

Going without [sleep | needsSleep] changes what you dream. The longer you stay awake, the less the dream feels like yours.

There is [no end] to it. Some come back knowing things they did not know before.

worldAdventures.title: Adventures on the Map
worldAdventures.description:
Some world map squares carry a [???] marker. Stand on it, or face it, and [Investigate] to play a branching adventure written for that place.

It may end in treasure, a fight, a minigame, an [augment | healthAugments], a shift in [faction standing | peopleFactions], trouble with the law ([crime | lawCrime]), or nothing at all.

Your [leader | partyBasics] goes in, and some paths open only to a leader of the right [temperament]. Once answered, a square stays answered.

worldBologna.title: Bologna
worldBologna.description:
[Bologna] is in the game as itself, street by street, one city with no seams.

Every building has a door, and every door is a way in. Most are homes; some are [shops and inns | worldHouses].

The city is alive: townspeople, Bolognesi born there, animals on the pavements and in the parks, birds on the rooftops.

worldPlatformer.title: Platformer Maps
worldPlatformer.description:
On a [platform] stage the map becomes a side scroller: [left] and [right] walk, [space] jumps, [shift] runs, and jumping against a wall [kicks off] it.

Climb ladders with [up]. Your companions follow close behind.

worldFlying.title: Flying
worldFlying.description:
Flight carries you like an [airship]: any direction, over almost everything. [Confirm] lands you, and so does leaving the map.

It comes from skills. [Fly] works only on the [world map | worldMapPage]. [Wing Wander] lifts you and [Earth Ebb] brings you down. The [flying broom | vehicleBroom] is a vehicle and flies on its own.

worldConnections.title: The Map of Maps
worldConnections.description:
The world quietly remembers how every place connects to every other.

You never see it. But when the [auto explorer | partyAutoIdle] walks for you, this is how it finds its way.

worldTreasure.title: Chests and Treasure Rooms
worldTreasure.description:
What waits in a chest depends on how strong your party is ([median level | craftLoot]), how dangerous the place is and the [biome | worldBiomes] around it. An emptied chest [stays empty], in every savegame of that world.

Some entrances lead to [treasure rooms], handmade vaults that are always waiting behind the same door.

worldTechTree.title: Research and Discovery
worldTechTree.description:
Several trees of discovery, from Physics and Astronomy to Alchemistry, Arcane and Technomagica. A world without magic hides the magical ones, a world given wholly to magic hides the sciences.

The sciences follow real progress forward from 2001. The magical trees follow the rediscovery of lost magic, and [Theotecnical] follows the [Vatican | vaticanEmpire] rebuilding its faith around engines. Each tree has strange fringe branches too.

Researching a node consumes [crafting materials] and gives some back refined. The world remembers which [leader | partyBasics] got there first.

A node can raise [stats | partyAttributes] for good, for your main characters in every savegame of the world. Its money, experience and items go only to the party that discovers it first.

travelOverview.title: Fast Travel
travelOverview.description:
[Bus stops] and bus signs open the travel screen. Vehicles and some other places open it for their own transport. You pick the [destination]; what opened the screen decides how you go. Each stop shows how tough the [enemies | combatEnemyLevels] are around it.

By bus, train, taxi, camper or car you ride a [travel map] while a [countdown] runs, even through menus and fights. At zero you have arrived: step off to reach the place. Other transports take you straight there.

[Sleeping | needsSleep], waiting or [foraging | needsForage] on the way makes the trip pass faster. The countdown follows the real clock, so a journey left saved for long enough may already be over.

At the end of a trip by vehicle you can walk out onto the ground or stay on the world map. The vehicle is parked beside you.

See also [Tickets and Fare Dodging | travelTickets] and [Places of Your Own | travelOwnPlaces].

travelModes.title: The Thirty Ways to Travel
travelModes.description:
Dozens of ways to travel, each trading money against time. Each one serves its own places: the bus reaches every town, trains and helicopters only places with a station or a pad.

- [Walking] is free and slow. A [bicycle | vehicleBike] or a [horse] is quicker. [Car sharing] and the [camper | vehicleCamper] cost fuel instead of money
- [Bus], [train], [taxi], [boat] and [ferry] are the everyday fares
- [Flights], [limousines] and [private jets] are fast and expensive. [Cruises], [balloons] and [zeppelins] are slow and dear
- Then the exotic ones: [magic carpets], [dragons], [teleport circles], the [hypermetro | topicHypermetroTrain], [wormholes], [time machines] and more

The further you go and the grander the ride, the more it costs.

vehiclesOverview.title: Owning a Vehicle
vehiclesOverview.description:
A vehicle is yours when you hold its [item]: the key, the deed or the broom. That puts it in the [Vehicles] menu. Mounts need no item: any companion marked Ridable on the pets page can be [ridden | partyRiding].

Vehicles stay [parked in the world] where you left them.

Walk up to one to open its menu. Depending on the vehicle you can [drive | vehicleDriving], [fast travel | travelOverview], step inside, use its storage, [refuel | vehicleFuel], [repair | vehicleRepair] it, play the radio, [make camp | needsCamp] or pick up a bike or broom.

vehicleCamper.title: Vehicle: The Camper
vehicleCamper.description:
The largest vehicle and a home on wheels: beds, storage and a walk in interior. It refuels at any roadside pump and moves faster along roads.

[Fast travel | travelOverview] by camper costs [fuel | vehicleFuel], not money. You can also [drive it in 3D | vehicleDriving].

The [workshop | vehicleUpgrades] can fit it to float and dive, or to fly. In the 3D world, [C] dives and surfaces and [F] takes off and lands.

vehicleCar.title: Vehicle: The Car
vehicleCar.description:
Smaller than the camper and quicker on a journey. It has a small interior and a boot, refuels at any pump and moves faster along roads. [Fast travel | travelOverview] by car costs [fuel | vehicleFuel], not money.

Any [parked] car can be [stolen]:
1. Face it and press the action button.
2. Choose to steal it.
3. Beat the [lockpicking minigame | gamesLockpick], which needs a [lockpick]. A [skeleton key] opens it outright and is used up.

Succeed and the keys, and the car, are yours. Take the keys from a driver, from a [downed body | lawDowned] or out of a pocket, and their car opens without a fight.

Fail the lock, or let the owner see you drive off, and you are charged with [vehicle theft | roadTraffic].

vehicleBike.title: Vehicle: The Bike
vehicleBike.description:
Pedal powered, so it needs [no fuel]. Nimble on local maps, faster along roads, and light enough to pick up and carry.

It still wears out and needs [repairs | vehicleRepair] now and then. [Fast travel | travelOverview] by bike costs a small fare.

vehicleBroom.title: Vehicle: The Flying Broom
vehicleBroom.description:
Needs [no fuel], works indoors, and tucks into your [pack | gearBackpack] like any other item.

It [flies] over everything: walls, water, cliffs. It lands on anything you could stand on, rooftops and bridges included.

Roads make it no faster.

vehicleBoat.title: Vehicle: The Boat
vehicleBoat.description:
An inflatable dinghy. No fuel, no storage, [open water] only. You can [fish | gamesFishing] from it.

Keep it patched: a burst hull or lost oars leave you adrift. Repairs are done from the [Vehicles | vehicleRepair] menu.

The whole party climbs aboard, with the [pet | partyPets] in the stern.

vehicleStarship.title: Vehicle: The Starship
vehicleStarship.description:
A ship for the stars, with a huge tank and a full walk in interior. It [cannot] refuel at a roadside pump.

Every world gives it a look of its own, which you can reshape with [Change Appearance | galaxyShip].

It needs [no driver]. You fly it from the [star map | galaxyOverview].

vehicleFuel.title: Fuel
vehicleFuel.description:
The [camper | vehicleCamper], the [car | vehicleCar] and the [starship | vehicleStarship] burn fuel. The bike, the broom and the boat do not.

Buy fuel at [pumps]. Its price rises and falls with the world's [oil market]. The starship cannot use a roadside pump.

Watch the gauge while you drive. Running dry [strands you].

vehicleRepair.title: Vehicle Damage and Repair
vehicleRepair.description:
Vehicles wear down part by part. Some parts are [critical]: break the engine, the brakes or the steering and you are going nowhere. Others only make the ride worse.

Damage comes from what you hit, and a crash with another vehicle hurts the most, unless you swerve in time.

Repairs consume [crafting materials]. While riding, the vehicle's condition shows as an [HP bar] on the party HUD.

vehicleUpgrades.title: The Workshop
vehicleUpgrades.description:
Vehicles are improved with [crafting materials] in the [Upgrade] tab of their [repair screen | vehicleRepair].

Make them quicker off the line, faster on the road, sturdier, or give them a bigger tank. A sleeker build even shortens your trips across the world map.

The [camper | vehicleCamper] alone can be fitted with two special modules: one to float and dive, one to fly.

Each step up asks for rarer materials, from steel and plastic to things far stranger.

vehicleCrew.title: The Crew
vehicleCrew.description:
Your [leader | partyBasics] takes the wheel when a journey starts, and only the [driver] grows in that vehicle's [specialization | progressSpecializations].

Long hours at the wheel wear a driver down. When they grow too tired, someone better rested takes over. Passengers doze when they need [sleep | needsSleep], and a [crash | vehicleRepair] jolts everyone awake.

Travelling together is good [company | needsSocial] and good [fun | needsLeisure]. A lone traveller misses out.

On the [starship | vehicleStarship] the crew looks after itself, eating from the hold as it needs.

vehicleDriving.title: Driving in 3D
vehicleDriving.description:
Every [vehicle you own | vehiclesOverview] can be driven across the [3D world | worldVoxelWalk]: the same lands, the same roads, the same distances.

Controls:
- [W] throttle, [Shift] turbo, [S] brake and reverse
- [A] and [D] steer, [space] handbrake, the [mouse] looks
- [middle mouse button] or [R3] swaps between the wheel and a chase camera
- [E] gets up and walks the cabin
- [H] shows the controls, [M] changes the map view

Asphalt, mud, sand and snow all handle differently, and the handbrake lets you drift. [Traffic | roadTraffic] shares the road with you and can be crashed into.

On foot your leader holds their equipped [weapon | combatVoxel].

roadTraffic.title: Traffic, Roadkill and Theft
roadTraffic.description:
Cars on the map are solid and dangerous. Get under a moving one and you are [run over]. Town traffic slows for people; highway traffic does not.

Being hit knocks you clear and causes an [accident]. People hit by cars carry their injuries afterwards, and a creature hit hard enough dies.

Run someone down and every member of your party falls in their eyes, and you are wanted for a [hit and run | lawCrime]. Keep ramming a creature and sooner or later it turns and fights.

A car whose driver has stepped out sits [parked and stealable | vehicleCar] until they return.

peopleOverview.title: People Are Real Here
peopleOverview.description:
Everyone you meet is a whole person:

- a [personality] that colours how they speak
- [traits | partyTraits], just like your own characters
- beliefs and [politics | peoplePolitics]
- money, skills, belongings and gear
- a [faction | peopleFactions], a home, a job and a daily routine
- a [backstory | societyHistory] rooted in your world's history
- a [medical history | healthDiseases] of old illnesses and scars

Some of the population is [animals]. Beasts have no job, no money and no opinions to share: they answer in their own voice.

peopleEmpathize.title: The Empathize Panel
peopleEmpathize.description:
Talk to someone properly and the [Empathize] panel opens. Its tabs show who they are: their life, their routine, their health, their loves and the people around them.

From there you can:
- [Socialize]: praise, insult, tell a joke and more
- give a [Gift] or [Trade]
- [Court | peopleOpinion] them, and in time [Propose]
- ask them to [Join Party | partyRecruiting]
- bribe, [pickpocket | econStealing], attack or challenge them to a [card duel | minigamesCardTables]

More is grouped by subject: [Beliefs and Politics | peopleCivics], [Money and Work | peopleDeals], and [Help, Games, Romance and Talk | peopleHelping].

[Propose] only works when they are truly drawn to you. Choose the kind of relationship that suits them, and they may become your partner.

Each party member has their own [standing] with each person, and only the one talking changes theirs.

[Free Chat] lets you type anything and hear what they say back.

peopleOpinion.title: How Somebody Decides What They Think of You
peopleOpinion.description:
What someone thinks of each of your characters comes from a few things:

- everything you have [done] to them
- how well your [traits | partyTraits] and [beliefs | peoplePolitics] sit together, felt before a word is spoken
- how clean you both are ([hygiene | needsHygiene])
- the way you [look]

[Attraction] is something else. Talk, gifts and trade shape opinion; [courting | peopleEmpathize] shapes attraction, and charm and a wash help.

Courting someone who does not want it is noticed. Keep at it and it becomes a [crime | lawCrime].

peopleLives.title: People Have Lives
peopleLives.description:
Everyone's life goes on whenever time does, even while you sleep.

- they are born somewhere and [move] for their own reasons
- they meet, date, marry and part, usually with someone close to home
- they build [careers | econWork], change jobs as they age, and retire
- some fall foul of the law: [convictions | lawTrial], [prison | lawPrison] and [bounties | lawCrime] they still owe

Spend a year in [cryogenic sleep | needsSleep] and wake to a world that aged, married and buried its own without you.

peopleTalking.title: What People Say to Each Other
peopleTalking.description:
When two people wander close together, they stop and talk, one line at a time in thought bubbles. How it goes depends on what they think of each other and who they are, and every chat [nudges their opinions | peopleOpinion].

People busy in the same room trade a word or two without stopping. Every personality has its own voice, its own small talk and its own private thoughts.

A person's recent conversations can be read in their [panel | peopleEmpathize].

peopleSettlements.title: Settlements and What Happens To Them
peopleSettlements.description:
Every town has a pulse: how [prosperous], how [safe] and how [happy] it is. Jobs, crime, the nation's fortunes and how [wanted | lawCrime] you are all push on it.

When things tip, the town lives through an episode:
- a [crime wave] when safety collapses
- a [boom] or a [bust] when money runs hot or cold
- a [festival | peopleHolidays] when the town is thriving
- an [epidemic | healthEpidemics], rare and cruellest in miserable places

Everything feeds everything else: people out of work turn to crime, crime fills the prisons, and the ripples reach the [news | societyNews], the [stock market | econStocks] and the gossip on the street.

peoplePolitics.title: Politics
peoplePolitics.description:
Every hyperpower is ruled in its own way: theocracies, sultanates, divine pantheons, corporatocracies and stranger things. Each has its parties, its political class, a head of state, and a mood that can turn.

[Elections | powersElections] follow each power's own custom, from ordinary ballots to papal conclaves and [goblin | goblinHorde] moots where the loser may be eaten. Between them come scandals, protests, coups and revolutions.

Everyone you meet has political views, and the people in office are real: they work in the capital and can be met. Every town also elects its own [mayor].

[Politics] in the main menu shows who governs the place you stand in. Your party can join in:
1. [Found a party | powersOwnParty] of your own.
2. Win supporters with [campaigns | powersCampaigns] and in [conversation | peopleCivics].
3. [Run for office | powersElections] in a town, a nation or a hyperpower.
4. Sit in [the Assembly | peopleONU] for a power.

peopleFactions.title: Factions and Reputation
peopleFactions.description:
The world is split among many [factions], and each of your characters has their own standing with each one, from hated to revered. It shifts with the [contracts | econQuests] you take, the [crimes | lawCrime] you commit and the sides you choose.

Some factions are branches of a [hyperpower | peoplePolitics]. Goodwill with a branch also counts with the power above it.

Standing matters. The faction that holds the country sets your [shop prices | econShops], and if it truly despises you its shops will not serve you at all. It also decides what work you are offered, who will speak to you and which [seats | peopleONU] you may take.

[Your own faction]: press [Found a faction] on the factions screen to raise your own banner, one per world. Its members are your companions and the soldiers of your [army | societyArmy]. It can swear allegiance to a hyperpower and later stand alone again. Its standing is the feeling of the whole party, so no single companion can swing it. Founding it also brings your team into your [political party | powersOwnParty].

peopleONU.title: The Assembly
peopleONU.description:
Every [hyperpower | peoplePolitics] holds a seat in the assembly, which meets in [Brussels]: walk into the chamber to open the lobby. The [Chamber] program on the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS] lets you follow it from afar.

A party member can [take a seat] for a power that already thinks well of them. The seat earns them standing and a weekly [stipend] that grows with it. A character can join only [once], resigning costs far more than joining gave, and falling too far out of favour gets them dismissed.

Once a week you can attend a session. Delegations speak on each motion, then you answer:
- [Support] or [Oppose]: your seat votes that way
- [Amend]: a softer push in favour
- [Filibuster]: talk it out without taking a side
- [Wild]: a gamble that may swing the room either way

A [PSI roll | partyDiceChecks] decides how far your words carry. Friendly delegations listen, hostile ones do not, and the [Diplomacy | progressSpecializations] specialization helps. Then every seat votes, in the open or in secret.

[Grave motions], such as war, [theonuclear devices | theonuclearBombingNewYork] or the [goblin question | goblinHorde], go to the [Security Council] of the strongest powers, which decides whatever the floor voted.

How you vote wins and loses friends among the delegations and with your own power. A [ceasefire], a [white peace] or [sanctions] can change the course of a war. Sessions you skip still happen and enter the world's [history | societyHistory].

With [Kofi Annan] in the party, the lobby offers the chair of Secretary General instead: no vote, but mediation, the casting word on a tie, and better pay. The [Tourists | theTourists] hold a chair of their own and admit nobody.

lawCrime.title: Crime and Bounty
lawCrime.description:
Every crime adds to your [bounty]. The law depends on where you stand, see [Whose Law Applies | lawJurisdictions], and a bounty never crosses the border.

The bigger your bounty, the worse the world treats you. Shops charge more, then [ticket counters | travelTickets] and [job boards | econWork] turn you away, and in the end ordinary shops will not serve you at all.

Each crime also raises the [heat]: how hard the police are looking for you right now. When it runs high, officers give chase. Heat fades with time, and faster in the dark.

While nobody is looking for you, an officer does not know your face. Once the heat is on, stepping into an officer's sight is enough. They cannot see through walls and see less at night, so you can slip past behind them. Stopping to chat with one while wanted is asking for trouble.

Most crimes need a [witness | lawWitnesses], and witnessed crimes make the town less [safe | peopleSettlements].

You settle your record through the [police portal | lawPolice], or when you are [arrested | lawArrest].

lawPolice.title: The Police Portal
lawPolice.description:
The [N€police | hypernetNeuroPolice] application on the Hypernet lets you settle your [record | lawCrime] before you are caught.

- [case file]: every charge with its fine, paid one at a time or all at once
- [self-report]: confess something not yet on file, at [half] the usual fine
- [custody]: turn yourself in, or ask for a hearing before [Eris | eris]

Both custody options take you away from the computer, to the [cells | lawPrison] or the [courtroom | lawTrial].

lawTrial.title: The Trial
lawTrial.description:
Justice is in the hands of [Eris | eris], and no two trials are alike. The courtroom, the gallery and even the case law she quotes are new each time.

Before the hearing you choose your [counsel]: hire an advocate, let a party member speak for you, or stand alone. The brief shows each one's skill, fee and your chances. Her [mood] can change everything, and in some moods she throws counsel out, with [no] refund.

Defending yourself, or letting a companion do it, teaches the [Law] [specialization | progressSpecializations]. A hired professional teaches you nothing.

The hearing runs from [plea] to [choices] to [verdict]. Innocent clears your whole [bounty | lawCrime]. Time spent with her away from the court builds a [bond | lawEris] that softens her, and a strong one may see the case thrown out before it starts.

One plea is [Challenge Eris], and it turns the hearing into a fight. At first nobody can die, and she even heals you. Then she fights for real.
- Win: your bounty never grows again in that world, and there are no more dates with her.
- Flee: you serve [a month] in [prison | lawPrison].
- Lose: the game is over.

Some defendants are special. [Bubba] seems to get off lightly. [Em | emTheMemoryWitch] does not, unless she has won Eris over on a date.

[Sandbox] mode has a reverse trial, where you play Eris.

lawPrison.title: Sentences and Prison
lawPrison.description:
A sentence comes in one of [2 shapes].

- a [fixed term] is served on the game clock. Press [OK] in the cell to sleep or wait it out, and your [bounty | lawCrime] is cleared on release
- an [open ended] sentence has no release date. Your bounty shrinks while you sit, and you walk out when it is gone

Turning yourself in at the [police portal | lawPolice] always means the second kind, with [no hearing].

On release, [Eris | eris] has a word for you.

lawEris.title: Dating Eris
lawEris.description:
You can take [Eris | eris] on [dates], and no two evenings are the same.

Each date happens somewhere in the world, and the [biome | worldBiomes] shapes it: a picnic, a seance, a stakeout and more. Her [mood] is never certain: playful, romantic, paranoid, prophetic, or worse. In her [eldritch] moods, things stop making sense.

She may break up the evening with [dares], some of them very much against the law. Two heartbeats on screen show how you are both doing. She feels differently about [every party member], and may turn her attention to one of your companions.

The first date that ends well brings a [blade seed | progressBladeSeeds].

societyMail.title: The Post
societyMail.description:
You can write to another party in the [same world], or to one in a [different world | worldsFolders] on your machine. The letter waits in their mailbox until someone plays them. Write at a writing desk and read at a mailbox, or do both through [Post Express] on the [hyperdeck desktop | hypernetOS].

You can hold a letter back for days, months or years. Write to your own party with a delay, and it becomes a letter to your future self.

[Money | econMoney] and [goods] can be enclosed. They leave your pockets at once and reach the recipient when the letter is collected. A letter can be read again, but it pays only once.

Post inside one world is [free]. Sending across worlds is very expensive, never less than [300,000 euros], and the price follows the market value of [oil] and [souls].

societyNews.title: The News
societyNews.description:
The world writes its own [news]. A fresh story arrives every morning, and the real events of 2001 land on their real dates.

Good news lifts a place's [property prices | econProperty] and fills its shops for a while. Bad news does the opposite.

Town troubles, riots, coups, elections, [epidemics | healthEpidemics] and the mayor's divorce all make headlines. Read them in the news reader on the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS], which needs a line.

societyDiary.title: The Party Diary
societyDiary.description:
The [diary] is your party's own story, written as it happens.

It remembers journeys, fights and bosses, friends made and lost, [evenings with Eris | lawEris], wounds and [augments | healthAugments], crimes and trials, [dreams | worldDreams], and much more. The small stuff, like idle chatter, is left out.

The party reads its own pages too: the newest entries become what they [talk about | partyBanterPage].

societyTopics.title: Conversation Topics
societyTopics.description:
Some words in dialogue are [topics], highlighted wherever they appear. Once one character hears a topic, [the whole party knows it].

A dialogue option that needs a topic stays [hidden] until you know it.

The [Topics] tab of this book lists them, and who knows each one.

societyArmy.title: Armies
societyArmy.description:
