You can recruit troops from a [faction | peopleFactions], and their number is shown over your sprite on the [world map | worldMapPage].

The [hyperpowers | peoplePolitics] march great armies under living leaders, factions guard their own lands, and free bands roam wherever they please.

Meeting an army never starts a fight on its own. You can talk to its leader, parley, attack or leave, and when two armies are already at war you can join either side.

A [field battle] plays out in real time: your units in [yellow], theirs in [red]. A fallen troop may survive badly hurt, or be [gone for good]. Units that lose heart slow down, weaken and may [rout].

You have three commander orders, each with its own wait:
- [Q] Rally: brings fleeing units back and lifts morale
- [W] Heal: patches up every wounded unit
- [E] Inspire: a short burst of full morale and fury

From the army menu, a [drill] splits your troops in two to train against each other. Nobody dies in a drill. Mercenaries in the party make the army cheaper to keep.

societyMultiplayer.title: Multiplayer
societyMultiplayer.description:
The multiplayer menu lists [local split screen], [LAN], [Steam] and [Online]. Steam and Online are not available yet.

[LAN]: one player hosts, the others find the game on the local network, and everyone plays in the host's world.

[Local split screen]: 2 players on one machine. Player two uses a gamepad, or shares the keyboard with WASD to move, E to act and Q to run. Player two takes one of the party members, and the rest walk on their own.

Either player can take over a member the computer is walking: player one with Tab, player two with the pad's X button or R. When the players are close, the two views merge into one.

From the split screen menu you can also start a co op [arena gauntlet | combatArena].

[Minigames | gamesOverview] can be played [hot seat] even without split screen, with a second gamepad or the numpad. In [arcade carts | gamesArcade] either player can steer, while chess, pool and bowling take turns.

During a [map battle | combatMapBattle], player two controls the second party member.

societyHistory.title: The Century Behind You
societyHistory.description:
Every world comes with a century behind it: an alternate history of Europe from [1900 to 2001].

It is full of coups, wars and assassinations, occult rites and paranormal anomalies, and the [Squishing | squishing] itself.

That past shapes the present: which [hyperpowers | peoplePolitics] rule and how strong they are, who sits on the [Security Council | peopleONU], what [epidemics | healthEpidemics] have swept the land, and what the people you meet have lived through.

The full story is in the [Historical Archive].

econMoney.title: Money
econMoney.description:
Money is [euros]. The only other currency is the [arcade token | econVending].

The [Assets] screen adds up your cash, [bank balance | econBank], [property | econProperty], [shares | econStocks] and [livestock | craftAnimals], takes away your debts, and shows your [net worth].

econShops.title: Shops
econShops.description:
Shops come in several kinds:
- [counter shop]: shelves sorted by category, restocked every day
- [daily shop]: fresh stock every day
- [teaching shop]: spells or skills to learn, changing daily
- [vending machine]: coded products, some of them very odd. [Appraising] training helps against the markup
- [Stockbusters]: the Hypernet marketplace. A courier brings your order, buying in bulk is cheaper, and the market adds its own tax

Prices shift with the maker's [share price | econStocks]. [Haggling] and good standing with the [local faction | peopleFactions] bring them down, and a [bounty | lawCrime] pushes them up. Shops buy from you for far less than they sell.

The keeper on shift remembers you. Buy often and their [opinion | peopleOpinion] of the party grows, until they start giving you a discount.

Many counters are staffed in shifts by townspeople, and the keeper on shift can be [recruited | partyRecruiting]. Their till then stands empty until someone new takes over the next day.

In a [zombie world | peopleZombies] some shops are abandoned for good, and the rest open only by day.

econStealing.title: Stealing
econStealing.description:
Anything on a shop's shelves can be [stolen]. The steal window lists the shops, stalls and vending machines nearby, with your chance on each item. What you take comes off the shop's own stock, so a shelf can be emptied.

Your odds improve with [DEX | partyAttributes], [Pickpocketing] training, darkness, a good [Stealth] look and an [Invisible | invisible] friend. Heavy and valuable items are harder. Even the best thief can be caught, and every attempt teaches you something, caught or not.

A till nobody is minding is free for the taking and no crime at all, unless its keeper left it to join your party. They will notice, report it, and think less of the rest of you.

Get caught and it is a [crime | lawCrime]. That keeper never serves you again, unless the shop is your own. In an empty world everything can be taken freely.

econBank.title: Banking and Loans
econBank.description:
The bank keeps your [deposits] and pays a little interest on them every week. It also [lends] money, one loan at a time, due in [30 days]. [Accounting] training lets you borrow more and pay less.

Interest keeps running while you walk, sleep, travel or lie in [cryogenic sleep | needsSleep].

[Pay on time]. Past the due date the debt grows every single day, until it is several times what you borrowed.

In an empty world the bank never opens.

econStocks.title: The Stock Market
econStocks.description:
The trading terminal lists [oil], [souls] and a host of companies. Prices move every hour, pushed by what happens in the world: booms and busts, [news | societyNews], [epidemics | healthEpidemics], the fortunes of the powers.

Besides buying and selling at market price, you can set [limit], [stop loss] and [take profit] orders.

Company shares pay a [dividend] every day, more in some trades than others, and more still if you own most of a company. Oil and souls pay nothing.

Shares held by townspeople are not for sale. In a [zombie world | peopleZombies] the market collapses.

The market reaches beyond the terminal: shop prices follow their makers' shares, the [oil price] sets what the [fuel pump | vehicleFuel] charges, and oil and souls set the price of a [letter | societyMail] to another dimension.

econProperty.title: Real Estate
econProperty.description:
Homes are for sale across the towns, from humble rooms to grand estates. What you buy in one savegame is off the market in every other savegame of that world.

Own a place and you can [rent] it to townspeople, who pay at midnight. Or rent one yourself as a [tenant]: you pay [3%] of its price on the [first of every month], and a missed payment gets you [evicted]. Selling brings back less than you paid, unless you have [Real Estate Appraisal] training.

A floor of a [procedural house | worldHouses] you own can be let too, and tenants will move in over time.

Prices rise and fall with the [news | societyNews]. In an empty world, property is worth nothing.

An [inn room] is different: you book it for a day and can extend the stay from the Assets screen. Busy inns fill up with tired townspeople. Forcing a room's door is [breaking and entering | lawCrime].

See also [Buying a Workplace | economyWorkplaces] and [Claiming Land | economyLandClaims].

econShopOwning.title: Owning a Shop
econShopOwning.description:
A shop you own belongs to the world: every savegame of that world finds it as the last one left it. Its book has pages for staff, shelves, stock and the warehouse.

- [roster]: pick who works the counter, from the party or the bench. The shop only sells while someone is on shift. Party members work for free, while someone from the bench costs [10 euros] an hour out of the till, which can go into the red
- [shelves]: fill them from your bags or buy from a wholesaler. Nobody restocks a shop you own but you
- [stock]: goods with recipes are made at the workbench from the materials in the [warehouse], and go straight onto the shelves

[Retail Management] training sells more. Each day a notice tells you what each shop made or lost.

[Crops | craftPlants], [eggs | craftAnimals], [honey | craftApiary] and [brews | craftBrewing] go straight to a shop of yours that deals in them. Deliveries run against a timer, and a late delivery pays half.

The [Tillbook] program on the [Hypernet | hypernetOS] lets you check on your shops from anywhere. Pricing, stocking and hiring are still done in person.

econWork.title: Work
econWork.description:
Dozens of jobs await, and any party member can be sent to work. Open [Job Offers] to see what is available now and where.

Each job lists the [stats | partyAttributes] it wants. Falling short never stops you. You simply do worse.

A worker [leaves] the party for the hours of the shift and comes back when it ends. A lone traveller works it out behind a fade. [Remote] jobs are done over the Hypernet from wherever you stand.

A shift comes down to a [d20 | partyDiceChecks] roll. Training in the trade helps your odds and your pay. A bad roll can be a [disaster] that costs money, hurts, or leaves its mark. Work also makes you [hungry | needsHunger] and [tired | needsSleep].

[Dress for the job]. Looking the part brings better luck and better pay: fearsome for fighting work, sly for crime, mystical for magic.

Shifts bring surprises: a rich customer, an inspection, a magical backlash. Armed jobs can end in an [ambush], a real fight with hazard pay if you win.

While you are [wanted | lawCrime] nobody will hire you, and a [faction | peopleFactions] that dislikes you keeps its jobs to itself.

econQuests.title: Quests
econQuests.description:
Every town has a quest board, and what it offers depends on where it stands. A job might send you to far coordinates, to [dig | worldDigging] up a buried site, to [land | galaxyLanding] on another planet, to hunt a dangerous beast or to question a citizen through [Empathize | peopleEmpathize].

Read the [terms] before you accept: reward, deadline and what failure costs you. Not every poster is honest.

The [Contracts] tab tracks what you have signed. The [Posted] tab lets you pin up a notice of your own, paying the reward in advance.

When you hand a quest in, the [KP | progressKnowledge] comes at once. The money and goods arrive by [post | societyMail], so visit a mailbox. Your [quest log] keeps every note in order, from To Do to Done.

econNotices.title: Reading a Notice
econNotices.description:
A notice is written in the [voice] of whoever pinned it up: a corporate contract, a goblin scrawl, a redacted military bill, a nervous private plea.

Read between the lines. What is left out, what is over explained and what is plainly a lie can all be spotted before you accept. The [terms | econQuests] panel gives the plain numbers.

econVending.title: Arcade Tokens
econVending.description: [Arcade machines | gamesArcade] take [tokens]. Buy them with euros at a converter machine or at the [Token Exchange | hypernetTokenExchange] on the Hypernet. Unused tokens can be cashed back in at the same rate.

craftThinker.title: The Workbench
craftThinker.description:
The [Thinker | topicThinkerMenu] is your general workbench, for [assembling] things and [dismantling] them. Every recipe is written on the item itself. Food is not made here: cook it in the [kitchen | craftCooking].

You can read a recipe once you have made it, if it is a starter recipe, or once your [training | progressTraining] in its trade is good enough. Harder recipes need a more skilled hand, and an unsteady one can botch a build and waste materials.

Raw materials come from taking the world apart: [felling trees | worldTerrain], mining rocks, breaking furniture, salvaging gear.

craftForge.title: The Forge
craftForge.description:
Every weapon and armour in the game hangs on the [forge] board from your first visit. Your [training | progressTraining] decides which of them you can actually make.

Each piece belongs to a trade: a robe to Tailoring, a rifle to Gunsmithing, a wig to Wig Making, and more. Cheap pieces can be made by anyone.

No two forged pieces are alike. Skill, good materials and the mood of the fire all leave their mark. Pick a [finish] before you forge and it stays on the piece.

[Smelt] melts a carried piece back into some of its materials.

The party switcher picks who stands at the anvil and who earns the [specialization | progressSpecializations] points.

craftAlchemy.title: Alchemistry
craftAlchemy.description:
Every alchemical recipe is open to you from the start, whatever your [class | partyClasses].

Copy a recipe onto a [bench], then edit and run it there. Change the steps too far and the batch is ruined. The better trained the alchemist, the safer the brew, and a true master may get extra flasks.

Reagents are paid when the bench starts, so cancelling refunds nothing. A batch cooks in game time, while you walk, work, travel or sleep. Set a bench to [repeat] and it keeps buying reagents until you run short of money.

craftCooking.title: Cooking
craftCooking.description:
The pot combines [2 recovery items] into one meal that the whole party eats at once. The order you add them in matters. Then the cook tries their luck: a fine hand makes a feast, a clumsy one burns it.

Two of the same thing make a dish with a surprise twist. [Raw meat] and [plant matter] can be eaten raw, at a risk, or cooked into something better.

Carrying [cookware], like a pot or a set of utensils, improves every dish.

The [Recipes] tab makes a dish from its written recipe and puts it in your pack. Without enough [Cooking] skill it may come out spoiled. You are warned first if a meal would set off someone's allergy.

craftBrewing.title: Brewing
craftBrewing.description:
Load a barrel and leave it. Brews ferment on the [world clock | worldWeather], even while you are far away, and slowly mature until they are [ready]. Training in [Brewing] or [Distilling] makes them finish sooner and yield more, and a little care at the barrel helps too.

An old barrel you stumble on may already hold something somebody left half done.

The [Grange] program on the Hypernet shows every barrel, [hive | craftApiary], [plot | craftPlants] and [animal | craftAnimals] you keep: what is ready, what is spoiling, what wants feeding. The work itself is still done in person.

craftFurniture.title: Building and Furniture
craftFurniture.description:
The [Build] menu places furniture on the grid. Its tabs also lay walls and terrain, set down whole houses, sell [animals | craftAnimals] and hold the [town charter | craftingTownFounding].

[Construct] pays in crafting materials, [Purchase] pays in money. [Dismantling] a piece gives back most of its materials, along with anything stored inside.

The [Homely] catalogue on the Hypernet delivers furniture to your [Stock]. Break a delivered piece and it is gone.

Placed furniture works: beds sleep, showers wash, stoves cook, a computer boots the [Hypernet | hypernetOS], a [piano | gamesPiano] or an [arcade cabinet | gamesArcade] plays, chests store. Chairs and couches can be sat on.

Building on someone else's land is [illegal construction | lawCrime], and you will be charged for it. You cannot build on the [world map | worldMapPage].

craftPlants.title: Farming
craftPlants.description:
Any [tilled soil] can be farmed. Plants follow the [season] and the [weather | worldWeather]: rain helps, snow slows them, and out of season they sleep. A [greenhouse] keeps them growing all year.

Crops keep growing while you are away, and you are told when one comes ripe. [Farming] training brings more off the same plot, and a [Plant Mage | partyClasses] in the party makes harvests far richer.

If you own a [shop | econShopOwning] that deals in produce, the harvest goes to its warehouse.

Fields on [procedural maps | worldProcedural] can be farmed too, and some are already sown when you find them.

craftAnimals.title: Animals
craftAnimals.description:
Buy animals in the [Build | craftFurniture] menu and set them on a tile. Manage them from the [Assets] screen: collect from them, sell them, or keep one as a [pet | partyPets].

They grow from young to adult, and adults give: an egg, a pail of milk, a fleece. A [Plant Mage | partyClasses] in the party makes them give more.

Keep them [fed] with the Feed action of the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel. A hungry animal stops producing.

Spending time with an animal lifts the party's [company | needsSocial]. Some, like dogs and donkeys, are kept just for that.

craftApiary.title: Beekeeping
craftApiary.description:
A hive is a living colony, from the queen down to the workers, and it gives [honey], [pollen], [royal jelly] and [wax].

Seasons and weather shape it, [disease] and [pests] threaten it, and it thrives or sulks depending on how you keep it. A harvest leaves the bees enough to live on. [Beekeeping | progressSpecializations] training gets you more from every hive.

In spring a crowded colony may [swarm], with half of it flying off behind the old queen.

craftArtifacts.title: Procedural Artifacts
craftArtifacts.description:
[Artifacts] are one of a kind items, weapons and armour, each with its own story. You find them in [loot | craftLoot], in [vaults | galaxyPatrons], at the end of [adventures | worldAdventures], and through certain rites.

One rite turns a [party member | partyBasics] into a weapon.

craftLoot.title: How Loot Is Rolled
craftLoot.description:
The stronger your party and the more dangerous the place, the better the loot. The deeper floors of the [Omega Tower | worldDungeon] pay the richest of all.

The [biome | worldBiomes] decides what kind of thing turns up: a laboratory gives components and medicine, a crypt gives charms. Some chests hold only a [keepsake]. [Appraising | progressSpecializations] training helps you pick the best out of the pile.

Item names are coloured by their [rarity | gearRarity]. A [Holy Patron Bunker | worldStructures] or a [patron's vault | galaxyPatrons] is worth the search.

craftContainers.title: Containers
craftContainers.description:
Chests, cupboards and crates hold whatever their owner kept in them. Once you empty a chest it stays empty, in every savegame of that world.

The [extradimensional container | gearContainers] opens anywhere, holds anything and travels with you. Your [camper | vehicleCamper] and [car | vehicleCar] have holds of their own, and storage [furniture | craftFurniture] you build is always yours.

Emptying a cupboard in somebody's home is [theft | lawWitnesses], and the more you take, the worse the charge if anyone notices.

The [Holdall] program on the [Hypernet | hypernetOS] moves items between the extradimensional container and your vehicles.

galaxyOverview.title: The Star Map
galaxyOverview.description:
The star map zooms out from the system you are in to the galaxy and far beyond, to the edge of the observable universe.

[Drag] to orbit, use the [wheel] to zoom. Click a body to see what you can do: [travel | galaxyTravel] there, or [land | galaxyLanding].

Every planet has its own day and night, so the hour you land at depends on where you land.

galaxyTravel.title: Travelling Between Stars
galaxyTravel.description:
Select a system and [travel] to it. Every journey burns [fuel | vehicleFuel], and fuel sets how far you can go.

You can only refuel at an ordinary living [star | galaxyBodies]: dead stars and black holes will not do. Press [Refuel] and the ship either starts the pumps or plots a course to the nearest star that can fill you up.

Aboard the [ship | galaxyShip], the [windows] always show where you really are.

galaxyShip.title: Your Starship
galaxyShip.description:
Every world starts with its own starship, always the same one for that [world | setupWorldCreation].

From the [vehicle menu | vehiclesOverview] you can redesign it from scratch, or change single features and keep the rest.

Under way the [crew | vehicleCrew] looks after itself: a meal, a wash, a chat, a game, a shift of sleep. Meals come out of the food in the hold.

galaxyLanding.title: Landing
galaxyLanding.description:
From orbit you can [land]. Pick a landing site if the world has any, otherwise you touch down wherever you are.

Alien surfaces are strange places to explore. Before you go, keep in mind:

- the danger depends on the [planet itself], not on your party. Read its [biosignature] before you commit
- there is [nothing to forage | needsForage]. You eat what you hunt
- a world stripped of its resources [stays stripped]

New species you meet go into the [bestiary | combatBestiary].

galaxyAnomalies.title: Anomalies
galaxyAnomalies.description:
Star systems hide [anomalous worlds], marked with a [?] on the map.

Hold orbit over one and you may [investigate], but only once. What follows is a [strange encounter | worldAdventures] that might leave you with a relic, some salvage, a fight with something native, or nothing at all.

galaxyBodies.title: What Is Out There
galaxyBodies.description:
The sky is full of [stars] of every kind, from ordinary suns to strange remnants and stranger things. Some systems hold two stars or more.

[Black holes] lurk out there and cannot [refuel | galaxyTravel] you. [Rogue planets] drift alone between the stars. Famous nebulae like the Horsehead and Orion sit where they should, and somewhere a [Dyson sphere] waits.

Our own [solar system] is all here, belts and [orbital debris | kesslerSyndrome] included.

galaxyPatrons.title: Patron Worlds
galaxyPatrons.description:
Some worlds in the Milky Way are named after the people who paid for the game. They are habitable, they circle rare and exotic objects, and the star map lists them under [Patrons].

Each of those people also owns a [hatch] hidden somewhere on the [world map | worldMapPage]. Below it lies their [vault], deep cellars full of rich [loot | craftLoot].

Once a patron proves their coordinates, the vault opens for that whole world, and a few gifts come with it.

The [Holy Patron Bunker | worldStructures] is a different place: a rare structure anyone might find at the bottom of an ordinary stairway.

galaxySky.title: The Night Sky
galaxySky.description:
A [night sky chart], separate from the [star map | galaxyOverview], with the constellations traced over the stars.

Press [Tab] to switch between the European and the Chinese sky, which see different figures in the same stars.

hypernetOS.title: The Hypernet Desktop
hypernetOS.description:
A computer desktop of the period: taskbar, start menu, windows and a handful of programs.

The Hypernet tile of the main menu opens your [hyperdeck | hypernetHyperdeck], which has to boot first. A computer in the world opens the desktop straight away. Files you write and settings you change are kept.

Online programs need a [line]: the [browser | hypernetBrowser], the shops, the bank, the [TV guide | hypernetTVGuide], mail and more. The tray icon shows whether you are connected. Deep underground, in caves or on alien worlds you are cut off, though your [starship | vehicleStarship] is always online. Offline programs like [Notepad | hypernetNotepad] and [My Computer | hypernetMyComputer] always work.

- [WASD] or [arrows] move the focus ring, [Tab] cycles
- [Enter] activates, [Escape] leaves a text field, then closes the window, then exits
- on a controller: [d-pad] navigates, [A] activates, [B] closes, the [left stick] is a free cursor

hypernetBrowser.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
hypernetBrowser.description:
Hypernet Explorer, the browser: tabs, an address bar, favorites, history, search and everything else a browser of the time had.

Reading teaches. Linger on a page long enough to actually read it and it pays a little [KP | progressKnowledge], once per page. Clicking through pays nothing. Your total is told when you put the [deck | hypernetHyperdeck] away.

The browser needs a [line | hypernetOS].

hypernetMyComputer.title: App: My Computer
hypernetMyComputer.description:
The file explorer: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or a program has written. Copy, move, make folders, throw things in the Recycle Bin.

Opening a file picks the right program for it: text in [Notepad | hypernetNotepad], pictures in Paint, and so on. For anything else, like a page saved from the [browser | hypernetBrowser], you are asked which program to use.

hypernetNotepad.title: App: Notepad
hypernetNotepad.description: A plain text editor. Notes typed here are kept in your [files | hypernetMyComputer], where other programs can read them too.

hypernetControlPanel.title: App: Control Panel
hypernetControlPanel.description:
The machine's settings, on three pages.

[System Specs] shows the computer you are using. On the [hyperdeck | hypernetHyperdeck], those are the parts you fitted yourself.

[Applets] holds the small settings programs. [Desktop Wallpaper] picks the background.

hypernetTVGuide.title: App: TV Guide
hypernetTVGuide.description:
The television listings. Pick a channel on the left to see its programmes, each with its tone and cast.

Select a programme to watch it play right on the [desktop | hypernetOS]. It is never quite the same twice.

For the weekly schedule and the studio, see [Television | hypernetTV].

hypernetObjectIndex.title: App: The Object Index
hypernetObjectIndex.description:
A catalogue of every object known to exist, one dossier each.

The [left page] lists them by category, with a search box. The [right page] is the dossier: what it is, a little lore, its price, what it is made of, and its 3D model turning beside it. Click the model to see it full screen.

If the marketplace sells it, you can order it from here. [Randomize] retells the lore in other words.

hypernetNeuroPolice.title: App: N€police
hypernetNeuroPolice.description:
The continental police portal, for settling your [criminal record | lawCrime] before they come for you.

- [case file]: pay your fines, one charge at a time or all at once
- [self-report]: confess something they do not know about yet, for a lighter fine
- [custody]: turn yourself in, or ask for a [hearing | lawTrial] before Eris

Custody shuts the computer down: the cells and the courtroom are real places you walk to.

hypernetEurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
hypernetEurodemics.description:
The public terminal of the continental [epidemic observatory | healthEpidemics].

- [situation]: how bad things are across the continent, and where you stand
- [outbreaks]: every outbreak still burning, town by town
- [archive]: outbreaks that have ended, and the great epidemics and mass hysterias of the past century

hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.description:
A catalogue of the [artifacts | craftArtifacts] in this world. Filter by type or search by name.

Each entry tells you whether you hold it or it is still out there. Select one to read its stats and its history: who found it, made it, dug it up or stole it, and when.

hypernetTokenExchange.title: App: Token Exchange
hypernetTokenExchange.description: Turns [euros | econMoney] into [arcade tokens | econVending] and back, at the same rate as the converter machines.

hypernetPhone.title: The Hexphone
hypernetPhone.description:
The party carries a mobile phone, with [credit], [contacts], [call history], an [inbox] and a couple of [games].

Call a contact and see what they do. Incoming calls let you answer or decline.

[Keypad digits] dial and act as shortcuts, [Enter] selects and calls, [Escape] hangs up and goes back.

[Payphones] share your contacts and credit, but only call out.

hypernetTV.title: Television
hypernetTV.description:
Tune a television and choose how to take it. [Listen] plays the broadcast where you stand. [Watch] takes you into the channel's [studio], where the cast turn to face you, and brings you back at the end.

The broadcasts know your world: the [history channel | societyHistory] and the [news desk | societyNews] talk about what has really happened. The schedule changes week by week and the words change every time.

[OK] moves to the next line, [Cancel] switches off. Commercial breaks sell real goods, or a political message.

Watching to the end is good fun for the party, though a [Technophobe | partyTraits] would rather not.

hypernetRadio.title: The Radio
hypernetRadio.description:
Radios tune across the [AM], [FM] and [EM] bands. Every song in the game is playing somewhere on the dial.

[Left] and [right] change frequency, [up] and [down] change band, [page up] and [page down] scan, [Enter] marks a favourite.

The radio remembers the last station you tuned.

hypernetMusic.title: Music and Sound
hypernetMusic.description:
Choose your [battle music] in [Options | optionsMenu]:

- [Biome] plays the battle track of the place you are in
- [Selected Track] always plays the one you pick
- [Random] picks a new track for every fight
- [None] fights in silence

Out of battle, every land has its own music for day and for night. Whatever plays announces its title and artist.

[Footsteps] change with the ground underfoot.

gamesOverview.title: Diversions
gamesOverview.description:
Most games are played [where you stand]: the pool table, the bowling alley and the chess board are set up right on the map.

Games are fun for the whole party: playing lifts [Fun | needsLeisure], winning lifts it more, losing stings. Each game also trains its own [specialization | progressSpecializations]. Games of chance soothe a gambler's [craving | needsAddiction], win or lose.

A companion takes the other seat. Alone, a passer by might join you, and with nobody around you play against your own [subconscious].

[2 players | societyMultiplayer] can share almost every game.

The [Minigames] entry of the title menu lets you play any of them for free, without touching a save.

gamesArcade.title: The Arcade Cabinet
gamesArcade.description:
Arcade cabinets take [1 token] a play and keep a [high score] table for your initials.

Each cart is a full game: [Snake], [Manpac], [Hoppa], [Meteoroids], [Bubble Pop] and more.

gamesBowling.title: Bowling
gamesBowling.description:
Ten pin bowling, against the computer or player 2 in [split screen | societyMultiplayer]. A clean hit sends them all flying, a thin one leaves a split.

1. [Aim]: left and right move you across the lane, up and down angle the throw
2. [Power]: stop the swinging bar
3. [Spin]: stop the second bar to hook the ball left or right

[Cancel] steps back one stage.

gamesPool.title: Pool
gamesPool.description:
A full size pool table, against the computer or player 2 in [split screen | societyMultiplayer].

1. [Aim]: left and right swing the cue. Hold up or down while steering for fine adjustment
2. [Power]: stop the swinging bar
3. [Spin]: stop the second bar to put side spin on the cue ball

[Cancel] steps back one stage.

gamesBasketball.title: Basketball
gamesBasketball.description: A free throw shootout against a computer opponent. Bank it off the backboard, or watch it rattle out of the rim.

gamesChess.title: Chess
gamesChess.description:
Chess by the full rules, where every piece is a creature. Each world fields its own two armies.

[Normal] is chess by the book against the computer.

In [Chaos] you still follow the rules, but Black does not: it steals your pieces, transforms them and drops monsters onto the board. Taking pieces fills your [Cheat Meter]. When it is full, press [Shift] to break a few rules of your own.

gamesFishing.title: Fishing
gamesFishing.description:
Cast into any water that looks fishable. What bites might be a fish, some junk, or something that wants a fight.

- [Aim]: look around. A [ring] on the water shows where the cast will land
- [Power]: stop the swinging bar. Longer casts reach deeper water, where other fish live
- [Bite]: when the bobber plunges, press confirm in time to set the hook
- [Reel]: hold confirm to reel in, let go to give line. Keep the tension out of the red or the line snaps

gamesSurfing.title: Surfing
gamesSurfing.description:
Waves break along the beach a piece at a time, so the break rolls sideways.

Stay ahead of it to keep scoring. Fall behind and the ride is over.

gamesShooting.title: The Shooting Range
gamesShooting.description:
A target range for [bows], [projectile weapons] and [firearms]. Each handles just as it does in a fight.

The range [lends] you the weapon and takes it back at the door, so you can try before you buy.

gamesHorseRace.title: The Horse Race
gamesHorseRace.description:
Bet [arcade tokens | econVending] on a race, then watch it run. Up and down move along the race card, left and right change the stake, hold Shift to change it by ten.

Every horse has its own form, and the [odds] are honest: a short price is a real favourite.

gamesTournament.title: The Monster Tournament
gamesTournament.description:
A knockout monster tournament to bet on. Pick a fighter, place a bet in [tokens | econVending], and watch the fights your monster is in.

Every fight is fought for real, and [betting does not affect the outcome].

gamesGambling.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
gamesGambling.description:
[Slot machine]: three reels, staked in [tokens | econVending]. Up and down change the bet by 10, left and right by 1. Matching symbols pay.

[Scratch cards]: pick a ticket from the rack, at [10 euros] each, and rub the panels. Three matching symbols pay out.

[Tarot table]: the reader cuts the deck and turns the cards one by one. What they say is up to you to read.

gamesPiano.title: The Piano
gamesPiano.description:
A playable keyboard. The typing keys are laid out as two rows, whites below and blacks above. A gamepad and the mouse also work.

Playing it feeds the [Fun] need.

gamesLockpick.title: Lockpicking
gamesLockpick.description:
Picking a lock is a [falling block puzzle]. Key bits drop into the keyway one at a time. Fill a row from wall to wall and the lock turns.

If the keyway fills or time runs out, your [lockpick] snaps. Harder locks are faster and meaner. A [skeleton key] opens any lock at once and is used up.

You can pick the doors of homes at night and [parked cars | vehicleCar]. Be warned: it can count as a [crime | lawCrime].

gamesHyperTamer.title: HyperTamer
gamesHyperTamer.description:
A virtual pet on a tiny LCD screen. It hatches from an egg and grows up, and how well you look after it shapes what it becomes.

It lives in [real time], even while the game is closed. Feed it, clean up after it, give it medicine when it is sick and turn off the light when it sleeps. Answer its calls quickly.

Warning: it can [die of neglect]. A little guessing game cheers it up.

gamesCards.title: The Card Game
gamesCards.description:
A collectible card game with a [collection], a [deck builder] and [duels].

Each card is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour from the world, printed with five stats: STR, WIS, DEX, PSI and CON. Gear goes onto a monster already on the board. A few [effect cards] can halve, double, destroy or swap, and you own one of each from the start.

Build a deck from the cards you own. If you never do, you are handed the best deck your collection allows.

A duel is played on a small grid. Each turn you draw and place one card: a monster on a free tile, gear on your own monster, or an effect. When the board is full, every monster fights its weakest neighbour, and whoever has more monsters left wins.

[Booster packs] bring new cards, always with something better than common at the end.

You can also [capture] a wounded creature in battle as a card. The weaker it is, the better your chance, and your [PSI | partyAttributes] helps. A capture kills the creature, but the spoils still drop.

gamesRaman.title: The Raman Scanner
gamesRaman.description:
Carry the [Raman probe], or fit a probe head to the [hyperdeck], and curious objects gain an [Analyze] choice: statues, paintings, masks, fossils, old books and more.

Analyze draws the object's spectrum and names what it is made of. The first scan of each object teaches you something. Scanning it again does not.

gamesPeriodic.title: The Periodic Table
gamesPeriodic.description: The periodic table, with a few [esoteric elements] you will find in no real one. Select an element to learn what it is and what it is good for.

arcaneSurge.title: State: Arcane Surge
arcaneSurge.description: Sharply raises [INT | partyAttributes] and [WIS], but drains [MP | combatAP] every turn. Fades after a few actions.

berserk.title: State: Berserk
berserk.description: Raises [STR | partyAttributes] and lowers CON, and the afflicted lashes out at anyone, friend or foe. Fades after a few actions or can be walked off.

bleeding.title: State: Bleeding
bleeding.description: Drains [HP] every turn, though it cannot knock you out on its own. It lingers after the fight and stops after a while of walking.

blind.title: State: Blind
blind.description: Your attacks often miss. Fades after a few actions or can be walked off.

burned.title: State: Burned
burned.description: Drains [HP] heavily every turn, though it cannot knock you out on its own. It lingers after the fight and stops after a while of walking.

charm.title: State: Charm
charm.description: The afflicted turns on their own side. It fades after a few actions, a hit may snap them out of it, and it wears off on the map.

cold.title: State: Cold
cold.description: Your attacks deal [ice | elementIce] damage and [STR | partyAttributes] rises. Ice hurts you less, but [fire | elementFire] hurts far more. Fades after a few turns, or on the map.

confusion.title: State: Confusion
confusion.description: The afflicted attacks at random, ally or enemy. It fades after a few actions, a hit may clear it, and it wears off on the map.

shadow.title: State: Shadow Veil
shadow.description: Your aim suffers, but enemies pick you far less often. Fades after a few actions.

silence.title: State: Silence
silence.description: The afflicted cannot cast [Magic] skills, though other skills still work. Fades after a few actions, or on the map.

sleep.title: State: Sleep
sleep.description: The afflicted cannot act or dodge, but gets some real rest for the [Sleep | needsSleep] need. Any damage wakes them, and it fades after a few turns.

static.title: State: Static
static.description: Your attacks deal [thunder | elementThunder] damage, [STR | partyAttributes] rises and thunder hurts you less. Fades after a few turns, or on the map.

stun.title: State: Stun
stun.description: The afflicted cannot act or dodge at all. It passes after a turn or two.

unbalanced.title: State: Unbalanced
unbalanced.description: Your aim suffers, and some [martial techniques | gearMartialArts] hit much harder against you. Fades quickly, and a hit may steady you.

vulnerability.title: State: Vulnerability
vulnerability.description: Badly weakens [CON | partyAttributes]. It lingers after the fight and wears off after a while of walking.

wet.title: State: Wet
wet.description: Your attacks deal [water | elementWater] damage. [Fire | elementFire] hurts you less but [thunder | elementThunder] more, and you get a little cleaner for [Hygiene | needsHygiene]. Fighting on water soaks everyone. Fades after a few turns, or on the map.

immortal.title: State: Immortal
immortal.description: You cannot be knocked out, even at 0 [HP]. It lasts a turn or two.

poison.title: State: Poison
poison.description: Drains [HP] every turn, though it cannot knock you out on its own. It lingers after the fight and stops after a while of walking.

rage.title: State: Rage
rage.description: Raises [STR | partyAttributes], but the afflicted attacks a random enemy and will not take orders. It fades after a few actions, a hit may calm them, and it wears off on the map.

freeze.title: State: Freeze
freeze.description: Frozen solid: no acting, no dodging, no [Magic | combatAP] or [Skills]. Thaws after a few turns, or on the map.

paralysis.title: State: Paralysis
paralysis.description: The afflicted cannot act or dodge at all. Fades after a few turns or can be walked off.

lockedOn.title: State: Locked on
lockedOn.description: Your hits are almost always critical. Fades after a few actions.

hpRegeneration.title: State: HP Regeneration
hpRegeneration.description: Restores [HP] every turn for a few turns.

mpRegeneration.title: State: MP Regeneration
mpRegeneration.description: Restores [MP | combatAP] every turn for a few turns.

apRegeneration.title: State: AP Regeneration
apRegeneration.description: Restores [AP | combatAP] every turn for a few turns.

magicReflection.title: State: Magic Reflection
magicReflection.description: Magic aimed at you bounces back at the caster, though [Piercing | combatDamageTypes] spells still get through. Lasts a few turns.

protect.title: State: Protect
protect.description: You step in front of badly hurt allies and take their hits, though [Piercing | combatDamageTypes] blows still graze them. Lasts one turn, and ends if you cannot act.

provoke.title: State: Provoke
provoke.description: Enemies can hardly help targeting you. Lasts a few turns.

hide.title: State: Hide
hide.description: Enemies cannot pick you as a target. Lasts a few turns.

counterAttack.title: State: Counter Attack
counterAttack.description: You strike back at every physical attack aimed at you. Fades after a few actions, or if you cannot act.

statusAilmentBlock.title: State: Status Ailment Block
statusAilmentBlock.description: Shields you from the common ailments, such as [Poison | poison], [Sleep | sleep], [Confusion | confusion] and [Charm | charm]. Lasts a few turns.

inspired.title: State: Inspired
inspired.description: Your spells cost far less [MP | combatAP]. Lasts a few turns.

hot.title: State: Hot
hot.description: Your attacks deal [fire | elementFire] damage and [STR | partyAttributes] rises. [Water | elementWater] hurts you more, [Petro | petro] less. Fades after a few turns, or on the map.

divineShield.title: State: Divine Shield
divineShield.description: You take less damage of every kind and suffer no critical hits, though [Piercing | combatDamageTypes] attacks ignore it. Lasts a few turns.

deathMark.title: State: Death Mark
deathMark.description: You take more damage of every kind, and enemies flock to target you. Fades after a few actions.

perfectFocus.title: State: Perfect Focus
perfectFocus.description: Your hits are almost always critical, but your [CON | partyAttributes] drops. Lasts a few turns.

ethereal.title: State: Ethereal
ethereal.description: [Physical | elementPhysical] attacks pass through you, but every [element | elementsOverview] hurts far more. Lasts a few turns.

lifeLink.title: State: Life Link
lifeLink.description: A bond whose purpose is not yet known. It lasts a few turns.

nausea.title: State: Nausea
nausea.description: Lowers [DEX | partyAttributes]. It comes from salt water, [overeating | needsHunger], early [pregnancy | partyReproduction] or [illness | healthDiseases], lingers after a fight and passes after a while of walking.

drunk.title: State: Drunk
drunk.description: Your [AP | combatAP] drains away every turn. It comes from [alcohol | needsAddiction], a hit may sober you up, and it passes after a while of walking.

infected.title: State: Infected
infected.description: Drains [HP] heavily every turn, though it cannot knock you out on its own. It comes from dirty wounds and some [diseases | healthDiseases], lingers after the fight and stops after a while of walking.

floating.title: State: Floating
floating.description: You hover: [thunder | elementThunder] hurts more, [physical | elementPhysical] blows less, [Petro | petro] not at all, and [STR | partyAttributes] rises. Some aerial techniques punish it. Fades after a few turns, or after a long walk.

invisible.title: State: Invisible
invisible.description: Almost everything misses you, and foes rarely pick you. It also helps when [stealing | econStealing]. Fades after a few turns, and any damage breaks it.

oily.title: State: Oily
oily.description: [Fire | elementFire] hurts you terribly, and your attacks deal [cursed | elementCursed] damage. Fades after a few turns, or on the map.

dodge.title: State: Dodge
dodge.description: You dodge almost every attack and spell. Lasts one turn, and ends if you cannot act.

withdrawal.title: State: Withdrawal
withdrawal.description: Weakens body and mind: lower [STR | partyAttributes], INT and DEX, worse aim and dodging. It starts when a craving boils over and ends once your cravings calm down. See [Cravings and Withdrawal | needsAddiction].

grappled.title: State: Grappled
grappled.description: Held tight: much less [DEX | partyAttributes] and dodging, and physical blows hurt more. Lasts a few turns.

pinned.title: State: Pinned
pinned.description: Held on the ground: no acting and almost no dodging, and [holds | combatWrestle] land far more easily. Passes after a turn or two, and a hit may free them.

guardBroken.title: State: Guard Broken
guardBroken.description: Weakens [CON | partyAttributes] and WIS, and [guarding | combatCommands] no longer helps. Some techniques hit harder. Lasts a couple of turns.

winded.title: State: Winded
winded.description: Out of breath: lower [DEX | partyAttributes], slower [AP | combatAP] charge and a slow drain on MP. Lasts a few turns.

comboReady.title: State: Combo
comboReady.description: Your aim and your critical chance rise. Lasts a couple of turns.

vitalExposed.title: State: Vital Exposed
vitalExposed.description: Physical blows hurt much more and land critical more often. Lasts a few turns.

rootedStance.title: State: Rooted
rootedStance.description: Raises [CON | partyAttributes] and lowers DEX, and you cannot be [Stunned | stun], [Unbalanced | unbalanced] or made [Floating | floating]. Lasts a few turns.

flowState.title: State: Flow
flowState.description: You counter more often, dodge better and shrug off physical blows. Lasts a few turns.

chiBurn.title: State: Chi Burn
chiBurn.description: Slowly drains [HP], dulls [INT | partyAttributes] and slows [AP | combatAP] charge. Lasts a few turns.

concussed.title: State: Concussed
concussed.description: Dazed: lower [INT | partyAttributes] and WIS, and worse aim. Lasts a few turns.

worldVoxelWalk.title: Walking the 3D World
worldVoxelWalk.description:
The [3D world] is the same Europe as the world map, built in cubes. Reach it on foot with [Liminal walk] in the world map travel menu, when you are not riding anything, or by stepping out of a vehicle you [drive in 3D | vehicleDriving].

[WASD] walks, the [mouse] looks, [Shift] runs, [space] jumps, [Ctrl] or [C] crouches. In deep water jump kicks up and crouch dives. If the leader knows the [Fly | worldFlying] skill, [double tap] jump to take off and again to land.

The [middle mouse button], or [R3] on a controller, swaps first and [third person].

[E] does whatever is in front of you: talk to a [shopkeeper | econShops] or a passer-by, loot, open a chest, [fish | gamesFishing], [fell | worldTerrain] or mine, ride a lift, or climb into your vehicle. Shopkeepers stand under a blue roof. [Chests | worldTreasure] pay out as they do elsewhere, and better underground.

[Esc] opens the party menu, and its return to the world map entry is how you leave. [Shift] and [R] opens the wait menu, [Shift] and [H] this book, [H] the control list, [M] cycles the map views.

Time runs fast out here, and the 2D maps catch up when you leave. Keep an eye on the sky around midnight: now and then something that is not a bird crosses it.

With [VR Headset] turned on in the Experimental tab of [Options | optionsMenu], an Enter VR button appears whenever a headset is connected.

worldVoxelDigging.title: Digging and Building in 3D
worldVoxelDigging.description:
In the [3D world | worldVoxelWalk] the ground is made of cubes, and you can take it apart. Hold the [left mouse button] to strike the cube under the crosshair with whatever the leader holds. Bare hands work too, just slower, and a gun or bow digs from afar. The deepest rock never gives.

Broken cubes go onto the [block bar] at the bottom of the screen, not into your bags. When it is full, build something before you dig more.

Hold a block and click, or press [G], to place it where you aim. Build to bridge a ravine or climb a cliff. Ore seams are different: they drop straight into your bags as crafting materials.

The bar has four views, switched with [Shift] and [Tab], or [L1]:

- [Blocks]: your weapon and what you dug
- [Items]: your quick bar favourites
- [Spells]: the leader's [battle skills | progressLoadout]. Attack spells blast craters, and one that hits a creature starts a [fight | combatVoxel]
- [Vehicles | vehiclesOverview]: call one of yours to stand in front of you

The [wheel] or [Q] steps through the cells, [1] to [9] pick one.

What you dig stays dug. Under the towns run old brick [sewers], some reached through iron manhole covers in the road, and [caves] wind beneath the land. You cannot dig or build during a fight.

combatVoxel.title: Fighting in the 3D World
combatVoxel.description:
In the [3D world | worldVoxelWalk] there is no battle screen. Fights happen where you stand, in [real time]. A creature that comes close and sees you starts one, and so does a blow or spell that lands on it. Hitting an animal while [driving | vehicleDriving] only knocks it aside.

You play the [leader]. Your companions act on their own, choosing their own attacks, heals and revives.

- [left click], or [R2], uses the weapon
- [right click], or [R1], uses the cell picked on the [bar | worldVoxelDigging]: a spell, an item or a block
- [R] reloads a gun, otherwise raises a quick [guard]

During a fight you cannot dig, build or open the party menu.

If the leader falls, the next one standing [takes the lead]. Run far enough from every creature to get away. One that flees remembers its wounds.

A win pays like any battle, and the bodies stay for you to loot with [E]. If the whole party falls, the 3D world closes and [Death, Gravestones and Permadeath | partyDeath] takes over.

economyHologramCheck.title: The Hologram Check
economyHologramCheck.description:
In the [Deeds] menu, a place you own has a [Check] button: a [shop | econShopOwning], a home, a [workplace | economyWorkplaces], a [claim | economyLandClaims] or a [town you founded | craftingTownFounding]. It sends the party there as a [hologram], without really travelling.

As a hologram you are see through and walk through walls and people. Look around freely, but taking a door, stairs or the map edge ends the projection and puts you back where you stood.

While projected, the menu button asks whether to [end the hologram] instead.

worldScenery.title: Things You Can Use on the Map
worldScenery.description:
Out in the world, many objects do something when you face them and press the action button. A few examples:

- [fountain] or [hydrant]: drink, or wash up for [hygiene | needsHygiene]
- [pentagram]: refills everyone's MP
- [bed], [campfire] or [tent]: open the [sleep menu | needsRestWorth]
- [bench] or [chair]: sit down
- [stove]: the [cooking menu | craftCooking]. [Piano | gamesPiano]: play. [Gas pump]: [refuel | vehicleFuel]
- [map] or [globe]: the [world map | worldMapPage]. [Bus stop | travelOverview]: catch the bus

Crates, sacks and bins hold goods or rubbish, vases break open, and a glint of [gold] might be a hoard, or just fool's gold. Bones, books and weapons lying about can be picked up.

Shelves, statues, graffiti and signs all have something to say. Torches and lamps can be switched on and off.

Warning: breaking into a [grave] or coffin is a [crime | lawCrime].

worldAtlas.title: The World Atlas
worldAtlas.description:
The [Atlas] is a map of the whole planet, opened from the [World Map | worldMapPage] page of the menu. It does not move you anywhere.

Switch between [Powers], [Regions] and [Climate] with [Q] / [W], [Tab] or [L1] / [R1]. Click a nation to read about it: who holds it, its weather, its dangers and its past.

[Left] and [right] step back through the years, faster with [Shift] held. Go back far enough and you may see the world as it was before the [Squishing | squishing].

[Up] and [down] step through the nations. [Drag] pans and the [wheel] zooms.

combatHyper.title: The Hyper: Limit Breaks
combatHyper.description:
Every class has one [Hyper], a limit break with its own name. It is a desperate move, offered only when things go badly.

It wakes when a character is badly hurt [during] a fight. When it is ready, it appears in the command menu in place of [Defense | combatCommands] or [Reload | combatAmmo], and a notice tells you.

It unleashes one huge act true to the class: a sweep over every foe, a full heal, the fallen raised, and more. For that turn the user is untouchable.

Each character can use it [once a day]. A [Freelancer | partyClasses] borrows someone else's.

combatAmmo.title: Ammo and Reloading
combatAmmo.description:
Guns, bows and other ranged weapons hold a [magazine]. The rounds left show on the [Attack | combatCommands] command.

Each attack spends ammo, and fast weapons fire a [burst]. When the magazine is empty, Attack becomes a [Bash] with the weapon itself.

[Reload] fills it and raises your guard, but uses your turn. The magazine is [not] refilled between fights, so reload before the next one.

Some weapons carry a [special skill]. When you can afford it, it takes the Reload row and reloads as it fires.

gearMartialArts.title: Martial Arts and Weapon Schools
gearMartialArts.description:
[Fists], [claws] and [nunchakus] are martial weapons. They fill both hands, but you still fight with your body through them.

[Martial Arts] skills need your hands free, though martial weapons do not count against that. Bodies with more or fewer hands have their own way of fighting.

The [Gun-Fu | partyTraits] trait lets you use Martial Arts with a bow, sling or gun in hand, with a [free shot] after each one.

[Swordsmanship] skills need a melee weapon, and [Firearms] skills a ranged one. A skill you cannot use right now is greyed out.

elementInfusions.title: Infusion Spells
elementInfusions.description:
The three [Infusion] spells charge the [whole party] with an element.

- [FlameInfusion]: grants [Hot | hot] and raises STR
- [FrostInfusion]: grants [Cold | cold] and raises CON
- [ThunderInfusion]: grants [Static | static] and raises DEX

The state always lands, and your attacks carry that element while it lasts. Infusions act [last] in the round.

needsGrooming.title: Toiletries and Cosmetics
needsGrooming.description:
[Toiletries] restore [hygiene | needsHygiene] when used from the backpack: soap, shampoo, a toothbrush, deodorant and more. A relaxing bath kit even adds a little fun.

[Cosmetics] make you look sharper for a while, raising your [Substance] look: lipstick, perfume, hair gel, hair dye and the like. Different ones stack, and using the same one again just refreshes it.

partyMetamorphosis.title: Changing Your Looks
partyMetamorphosis.description:
A character can change their body and face after creation.

- [Metamorphosis Potion]: opens every body and then the face gallery. Use it on one party member from the [backpack | gearBackpack]. It costs about [250 euros] and can be crafted
- [Surgerybot Swarm]: the same, but only with bodies seen in this world. About [200 euros]
- at a [clinic | healthSurgery]: [plastic surgery] changes the body for [100 euros], [face surgery] the portrait for [50 euros]

If you leave without changing anything, the potion or swarm is given back.

partyFamiliar.title: Familiars
partyFamiliar.description:
A [familiar] is a creature bound to one character for good. It belongs to whoever called it, not to the party.

Cast [ConvokeFamiliar] to call yours. Your [class | partyClasses] decides what answers: a Necromancer meets something dead, a Mechanic something built, a Witch a bat or a ghost. The same character always meets the same familiar, and it grows with its owner's [level | progressLevels].

Once called, it [stays]. It walks with you and joins [every battle] as the fourth member. Some can be [ridden | partyRiding]: talk to it and pick Ride.

It leaves if it is [killed], if you [dematerialize] it, or if its owner leaves the party. You can call it back from the skill or the [Pets | partyPets] page, but not during a battle.

powersOwnParty.title: Founding a Political Party
powersOwnParty.description:
Your party can found [one political party] of its own in each world.

How to do it:

1. Open [Politics | peoplePolitics] from the main menu and go to the [Own party] tab. The [Propaganda2] program on the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS] works too.
2. Give it a name, or roll one. If you raised a [faction | peopleFactions], its name is suggested.
3. Choose an [ideology]. This is the only thing you must pick.
4. Pick up to [3 tenets], such as Liberty, Order or Arcana. Opposite tenets cannot be held together.
5. Set the [weekly fee] each supporter pays, from 1 euro to 10000 euros.
6. Confirm. Everyone in your party joins as a founding member.

A new party has [no supporters]. Win them with [campaigns | powersCampaigns], or one by one in the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel.

Every week each supporter pays the fee to you. The fee also decides [who joins]: a cheap one draws the poor, a steep one only the wealthy. Some supporters drift away over time whatever you do.

You can change the name, ideology, tenets and fee at any time, and with them who the party appeals to.

powersCampaigns.title: Political Campaigns
powersCampaigns.description:
A [campaign] spends money over days or months to win people to a party: yours, or any other. Run one from the [Campaigns] page of [Propaganda2 | powersOwnParty].

1. Choose the kind. A [conversion] wins people over. A [smear] shakes the faith of a rival party's supporters. Your own party cannot be smeared.
2. Choose the party, and where: the whole world, a town, a nation or a [hyperpower | peoplePolitics].
3. Choose how hard: leaflets at 20 euros a day, rallies at 100, broadcasts at 500, saturation at 2500.
4. Choose how long, from 1 day to 6 months.
5. Read the [projection], then launch. The whole cost is paid up front.

Crowded places cost more to reach. People who already lean your way are easy to win, the deeply committed are hard. A smear softens the ground for your next conversion.

powersElections.title: Running for Office
powersElections.description:
Any member of your party can stand in an upcoming election: a town's [mayor | peoplePolitics], a nation's government, or a hyperpower's head of state. Do it from the [Elections] page of [Propaganda2 | powersOwnParty].

1. Pick the candidate.
2. Pick the election from the list.
3. Press Stand and pay the [deposit]: 100 euros for a town, 2000 for a nation, 20000 for a hyperpower. It is never returned, win or lose.

Each member stands in one election at a time, and can withdraw before the vote. The [Holy Vatican Empire | vaticanEmpire] picks its head in a conclave and takes no outsiders.

With a [political party | powersOwnParty] behind them, your candidate carries its platform and its voters. Without one, they run alone as an independent. Voters lean toward whoever thinks like them.

Win a town and you appoint its guard captain, tax collector and high priest. Win a nation and you lead it, unless history already holds that seat. In the last days before a vote, [Endorse a candidate] in the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel to sway voters one by one.

peopleCivics.title: Talking Beliefs and Politics
peopleCivics.description:
The [Beliefs] and [Politics] groups of the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel let you work on what someone believes and how they vote.

[Beliefs]: preach your creed, debate theirs, ask their views, or pray together if you both hold a faith.

[Politics]:

- [Ask about their vote]. The wary keep it to themselves unless they trust you.
- [Join their party], or [Invite to your party | powersOwnParty].
- [Campaign for a party]: nudge their views. Charm and the Public Speaking [specialization | progressSpecializations] help.
- [Endorse a candidate | powersElections]: only close to an election.
- [Petition]: only for someone who holds an office.

A refusal cools them a little. Pestering the uninterested cools them more.

[Petitioning] the powerful can buy a [pardon | lawCrime] for your heaviest charge, for half its bounty, or a tax cut for their country, for 5000 euros. You pay only if they agree, and the better they like you, the likelier that is.

peopleDeals.title: Money, Work and Favours
peopleDeals.description:
The [Money] and [Work and travel] groups of the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel are deals with grown, thinking people. Most can be tried once a day per person.

[Money]:

- [Ask for stock tips] from someone who owns [shares | econStocks]. Not everyone tells the truth.
- [Trade shares]: friends give fairer prices.
- [Lend money]: 20, 50, 100 or 250 euros, owed back with interest in a week. The honest usually repay.
- [Borrow money]: only from a rich friend. It is taken back when due. Fail to pay and the friendship sours fast.

[Work and travel]:

- [Ask for work | econWork] at their workplace.
- [Hire] and [Fire] for a [shop you own | econShopOwning] in their town. Firing someone is not forgotten.
- [Work together]: a few hours beside them, for a share of the pay.
- [Ask for a ride], for a fare, or free from a good friend.
- [Borrow their vehicle] for a day. Lose it and they report it [stolen | lawCrime].
- [Invite to move] to another town, or [Invite to an expedition] on a [tower floor | worldDungeon].

peopleHelping.title: Helping, Games and Matchmaking
peopleHelping.description:
The [Help], [Games], [Romance] and [Talk] groups of the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel hold the kinder actions.

[Help]:

- [Treat them] with a healing item from your pack.
- [Give medicine | healthDiseases] for an illness they show.
- [First aid]: someone [downed | lawDowned] gets back on their feet, and is grateful.
- [Offer a fix | needsAddiction] to an addict. They will love you for it, and the habit deepens.
- [Intervene]: talk an addict toward quitting.
- [Offer shelter]: a [refugee | peopleHorde] or someone sleeping rough moves into a house you own.

[Games]: [Challenge to a game | gamesOverview] they know, for fun or for 5, 20 or 50 euros.

[Romance]: [Introduce to someone] matches two single people you both know. Maybe they hit it off.

[Talk]: [Rumours and news | societyNews] tells you what the world is talking about, from wars to the [Horde | goblinHorde].

partyRiding.title: Riding a Companion
partyRiding.description:
A pet, a follower or a [familiar | partyFamiliar] can carry you. Party members and children never can.

1. Open the [Pets | partyPets] page and switch the companion to [Ridable].
2. Press [Ride] on its row, or press OK facing it and choose Ride.
3. To get off, press OK on an empty tile and choose Stop riding, or press [Dismount] on the Pets page.

A familiar must be convoked to be ridden.

In the saddle you travel faster than on foot, roads on the world map go by quicker, and you can still talk, open doors and use what is around you. You get off at the camper door. Riding trains [Horse Riding | progressSpecializations] and Animal Training.

Other Ridable companions carry the rest of the party. Riding belongs to the ordinary maps and the world map, not the [3D world | worldVoxelWalk].

lawDowned.title: Downed People and Bodies
lawDowned.description:
A fight between people that ends with blunt blows leaves the loser [downed]: on the ground, crawling. Given time, they get up on their own.

Press OK on a body to see what you can do:

- a downed [person]: Loot, First aid, Coup de grace
- a downed [monster]: Coup de grace
- a [corpse]: Loot, Butcher

Taking anything from someone still breathing is a [robbery | lawCrime]. Their [car keys | roadTraffic] open their parked car.

[First aid] gets them up at once. No crime, and they will remember the kindness.

A [coup de grace] on a person is [murder] if anyone sees it, unless they were [wanted]: then you collect the bounty instead.

[Butcher] harvests what the body has to give.

The hurt heal in time, faster at a [clinic | healthSurgery].

lawStreet.title: Street Crime, Wanted People and Patrols
lawStreet.description:
Towns have crimes of their own. Pickpockets work the crowds, victims fight back, old grudges turn into brawls, and you hear about it as it happens. Pickpockets steer clear of anyone who looks [intimidating].

Every crime puts a [bounty] on whoever did it. A [wanted] person, or one with a warrant on the [quest board | econQuests], can be fought without it being a crime, and whoever brings them down collects.

When monsters wander into town, guards and the brave stand and fight. Everyone else runs.

[Patrols]: the hotter your [heat | lawCrime], the more officers walk the streets. They drift home as it fades.

Where the [Goblin Horde | peopleHorde] has ruled for a while, the streets are rougher.

peopleZombies.title: The Zombie World
peopleZombies.description:
In a world made with the [zombie | setupTimelines] population, most people are walking dead. They shuffle through the routines they had in life, but there is nothing left to say: [touching one starts a fight | combatBasics].

The dead are the same on every visit, and a zombie you [kill stays dead]. Flee instead and it is dazed for a moment.

Learn to tell them apart:

- [shamblers] are slow and short sighted
- [runners] see far and chase faster than you walk
- [screamers] wake every zombie nearby

And worse things crawl and lurk. Walls hide you from most of them, not all. A zombie that loses you goes to where it last saw you, then gives up.

peopleHorde.title: The Horde's Ground and Refugees
peopleHorde.description:
In a nation ruled by the [Goblin Horde | goblinHorde], the towns are full of [goblins]: ordinary citizens with names, jobs and homes, not enemies.

The longer the Horde holds a country, the rougher it gets: more [pickpockets | lawStreet], more brawls, fewer police, litter in the streets.

When the Horde [conquers] a country, those who will not live goblin lives pack up and leave, for a free country nearby or a [camp of tents] by the border. When the Horde [loses] one, the refugees slowly come home.

Give a refugee a roof with [Offer shelter | peopleHelping] in the [Empathize panel | peopleEmpathize].

progressSpellCrafting.title: Making New Spells and Skills
progressSpellCrafting.description:
All of this happens in the [Training | progressTraining] menu. Open a member's schools: the benches are on the right page, and each one spends the party's [KP | progressKnowledge].

Ways to make something new:

- [Fuse Spells | progressFusion]: melt two abilities into one, if the dice allow
- [Craft Spell and Craft Skill | progressWorkbench]: build your own from parts
- [Enchant Weapon, Equipment or Book | progressEnchanting]: bind a spell into gear
- [Write Skill Book and Write Grimorie | progressWritingBooks]: put what you know into a book, to teach it to others

[Hexorcize | progressHexorcize] works the other way, breaking magical gear back down into KP.

You can also learn existing abilities on a [school tree | progressAtlas], from [grimoires and skill books | progressGrimoires], from people in the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel, from some shops, or at the end of an [adventure | worldAdventures]. In a [world of chaos | setupTimelines], skills come on their own as you level.

A spell made on a bench belongs to its maker. Write it into a book to share it.

progressWorkbench.title: Writing Your Own Spells
progressWorkbench.description:
[Craft Spell] and [Craft Skill], on the right page of [Training | progressTraining], build a new ability from parts. A spell spends MP, a skill spends AP.

1. Pick a [core]: an [element | elementsOverview] like fire or ice, healing, a hard blow, an aimed shot, and more.
2. Pick an [amplifier] for more power.
3. Pick a [shape]: one enemy, all of them, an ally, yourself.
4. Add [riders] such as poison or a shield, and [refinements] such as never missing or casting twice.
5. Give it a name, a description, an icon and an animation.
6. Press Write.

[Roll it] fills every row at random, if you want a surprise.

Every part costs [KP | progressKnowledge] and makes the ability more demanding: harder to cast, and needing a stronger [stat | partyAttributes] from whoever uses it.

Name a spell in one [CamelCase | camelcaseMagic] word, like FireBolt.

You can rebuild an ability later, paying only the difference. [Unmake] deletes it for nothing back.

progressEnchanting.title: Enchanting Gear
progressEnchanting.description:
Three benches in [Training | progressTraining] bind a spell into a piece of gear. Only spells can be bound, never skills, and the caster keeps knowing it.

1. Open the bench.
2. Pick a piece you carry or wear.
3. Pick a spell and confirm.

The old piece is gone, and a unique new one takes its place.

- [Enchant Weapon]: an attack spell bursts out on every critical hit
- [Enchant Equipment]: a protective spell answers when the wearer is struck hard
- [Enchant Book]: any spell, cast for free whenever the book is read

Beware: an enchanted book may [burn] as it is read. A skilled [Enchanting | progressSpecializations] reader keeps it longer.

It costs [KP | progressKnowledge], more for stronger and stranger spells. A piece that already carries a spell cannot take another. [Unmake] destroys an enchanted piece for nothing back.

progressWritingBooks.title: Writing Skill Books and Grimories
progressWritingBooks.description:
[Write Skill Book] and [Write Grimorie], in [Training | progressTraining], copy what the party knows into a book. A skill book holds skills, a grimorie holds spells.

1. Open the bench and choose a few pages from everything your members know.
2. Check the price in [KP | progressKnowledge].
3. Press write. The book goes into your backpack.

Use it from the backpack. It opens like a [grimoire | progressGrimoires], offering exactly your pages. Hand each page to a member who does not know it yet.

The book is used up once every page has been taken. Close it early and nothing is lost: it returns to your pack, and the pages taken in that sitting are forgotten again.

This is how a spell [made on a bench | progressWorkbench] reaches the rest of the party.

progressHexorcize.title: Hexorcizing
progressHexorcize.description:
[Hexorcize], the last bench in [Training | progressTraining], breaks magical weapons and equipment down into [KP | progressKnowledge].

Only magical pieces in your pack are listed, so take a piece off first. Richer, stronger and [enchanted | progressEnchanting] pieces give more.

Pick a piece and choose [Unmake] for one copy or [Unmake All] for every copy. It cannot be undone.

hypernetHyperdeck.title: The Hyperdeck
hypernetHyperdeck.description:
The [hyperdeck] is a folding handheld computer the party builds itself. Open it with [P] or from the Hypernet tile of the main menu.

Click the screen to switch it on. Click the base to open the board, then drag [components] onto the grid. Components are items you buy, find or salvage, and fitting one takes it from your [backpack | gearBackpack].

- L1 and R1 or Tab turn a part
- [Auto fit] fills the board from what you carry
- [Case] picks a different shell, emptying the board back into your bag
- [BIOS] lists what is wrong

To boot, the deck needs a [processor], [memory], [storage], a [panel] and a [cell] strong enough to power it all. Hot machines want cooling.

Once it boots you reach the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS], and your parts show up in the [Control Panel | hypernetControlPanel]. Every party starts with a cheap second hand deck that just about works.

The [CHIP] button opens the [chip lab | hypernetChipLab], where you can etch a processor of your own.

hypernetChipLab.title: The Chip Lab
hypernetChipLab.description:
The [chip lab] is a bench where you draw your own logic and etch it onto a processor for the [hyperdeck | hypernetHyperdeck]. Open it with the CHIP button on the deck, or with the Circuit Board Editor on the [desktop | hypernetOS].

You draw on a grid with wires, torches that invert a signal, repeaters, bridges, gates, clocks and lamps.

- left button draws, right button rubs out
- pick a tile twice to change its settings
- Run, Pause and Step test the circuit
- ready made circuits can be stamped in

[Etch die] turns the drawing into a processor part, paid for in [salvaged steel]. More logic makes a faster chip, and a hungrier one.

A half drawn circuit waits on the bench for you.

hypernetCalendar.title: App: Calendar
hypernetCalendar.description:
A month to a page calendar on the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS]. It works without a line.

Each day shows the [public holidays | peopleHolidays] of the nation you pick, the coming [elections | powersElections] and the deadlines of your [quests | econQuests].

Add your own [appointments] with an hour and a note, and you will be reminded on the day.

minigamesCardTables.title: Card Games Against People
minigamesCardTables.description:
The [card game | gamesCards] can be played for real.

In the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel, challenge someone to a [card duel] or offer to [swap cards], once a day each. Someone who dislikes you refuses.

Before a duel, choose the stake: nothing, some money, or an item of yours against one of theirs. Walking out of a staked duel [forfeits] it. You need a deck of at least 9 cards to sit down.

[Hyper Card Arena], on the [Hypernet desktop | hypernetOS], pits you against the machine. Play a single match, or pay an entry fee of 10 to 300 euros for a knock out bracket of eight. Each win pays you back and more, and the title brings a prize. Lose once and the run is over.

galaxyRocketLaunch.title: Coilgun Launches
galaxyRocketLaunch.description:
From a [spaceport], a coilgun throws an armoured round into the sky. Pick where you leave from, the flight and where you come down.

You can leave from [Apulia | topicApuliaSpaceCenter], [Greenwich | topicGreenwitchSpaceCenter], the Omega Tower, your [starship | vehicleStarship] in orbit, or a patron's [vault | galaxyPatrons].

Fares:

- a hop between Greenwich and Apulia: free
- down from orbit: 200 euros
- up to the starship: 500 euros
- the Moon base: 1,200 euros
- farther wonders: 2,000 to 3,000 euros

You pay only when the flight starts. Flights to a vault and in the story are free.

On the way up the round crosses a belt of [orbital debris | kesslerSyndrome], worse in storms and at night. The autopilot always gets you through.

Press [F], or hold the pad's top button, to fly [by hand] and steer through the debris yourself. Warning: if the hull breaks while you fly by hand, the [whole party dies].

[Tab] skips to the next stage, holding [Cancel] skips to the arrival, [M] shows the chart.

partyOrigins.title: Origins
partyOrigins.description:
The last step of creation picks an [origin]: where and how the party starts. Every party also gets a few potions, a packed meal and a cheap [hyperdeck | hypernetHyperdeck].

- [Travel starts]: by train, camper, car or bike, out in space, stranded somewhere remote, or at the gate of the [Tower | worldDungeon].
- [Money and power]: a CEO with a fortune, a Mayor with a city, a Diplomat with a seat in the [Assembly | peopleONU], and more.
- [Armies | societyArmy]: lead troops of a faction, desert one, rule as a warlord, march with the Goblin Horde, or become goblins yourselves.
- [Gear starts]: an Arcanist with forbidden lore, a Mercenary with guns, an Augmented crew with [augments | healthAugments], a Card Collector with a [deck | gamesCards], and more.
- [Odd starts]: a [wanted | lawCrime] Criminal, a crash landing on a strange planet, a wake up in a bunker, and stranger things.

Some origins make the road ahead much harder.

pastimesReading.title: Bookcases and Reading
pastimesReading.description:
A [bookcase] holds a few books worth leafing through. Reading one gives the whole party some [Fun | needsLeisure] and, the first time, a little [KP | progressKnowledge].

Statues, paintings, masks and fossils reward a curious eye the same way.

Some shelves hold a real book you can [take], and any shelf can keep one of your own until you come back for it. With a [Raman probe | gamesRaman] you can also [Analyze] what sits there.

Readable books open in a book viewer. Drag a page to turn it, or fling it off the screen to tear it out. Enter leaves a bookmark, Shift jumps to the next one.

combatBestiary.title: The Bestiary
combatBestiary.description:
The [bestiary] remembers every creature you have crossed. A creature joins it the moment a fight begins, even if you run.

Each entry has three tabs:
- [Lexicon]: what it is, how strong it is, what hurts it
- [Ecology]: where and when it lives, in which [biomes | worldBiomes]
- [Extraction]: what it leaves behind when [harvested | combatCorpses] and how it fights

A turning model of the creature sits beside the page. Beings met on [other planets | galaxyLanding] fill an alien chapter of their own.

travelTickets.title: Tickets and Fare Dodging
travelTickets.description:
Buses, trains, ferries, flights and the faster lines all sell [tickets], and the clerk writes your name down. With a [bounty | lawCrime] on your head, or the police on your heels, nobody will sell you one. Taxis and your own vehicles never ask.

Short of money, you can choose [Travel With No Ticket]. The trip runs as usual, but an inspector may walk the aisle. A short hop is usually safe, a long trip rarely is. Getting caught means a [fare evasion] charge.

Fuel cannot be dodged: a vehicle without enough of it simply does not leave.

On the [Hypernet | hypernetOS], [Wayfare] lists prices and travel times for every stop, and [Hail] calls a taxi to wherever you stand on open ground. You can also ask a vehicle owner for a ride from the [Empathize | peopleEmpathize] panel.

travelOwnPlaces.title: Places of Your Own
travelOwnPlaces.description:
A vehicle needs no station. From the travel screen of the [camper | vehicleCamper] or the [car | vehicleCar], choose [Write down a place of your own], pick a square of the world map and name it. It becomes a pin only your vehicles can reach.

Mountains, open water, rivers and places that already have a name cannot be chosen.

Towns you [found | craftingTownFounding] become stops for everyone in your world, and an open [patron's vault | galaxyPatrons] adds a free station of its own. Some towns read [Offline]: still on the map, but no line goes there any more.

lawWitnesses.title: Witnesses
lawWitnesses.description:
Most deeds reach your [record | lawCrime] only if somebody saw them and chose to talk.

A witness has to see you: close by, looking your way, with nothing in between. Darkness and a leader with a good [Stealth] look make you harder to spot.

Your own companions never talk, and neither do people who like the party enough. A frightening [Intimidation] look can buy silence too. Police officers always report, and so does the [victim].

Taking things from someone's home is a gamble against the noise you make: heavier hauls are louder, and every pair of eyes or ears nearby makes it worse. If nobody can see or hear you, you simply get away with it.

Open ground, shops, inns, public buildings and your own places are never theft.

lawArrest.title: Being Arrested
lawArrest.description:
An officer who catches you offers a choice: [pay the bounty | lawCrime], [go to trial | lawTrial], read the charges, [resist arrest], [go to jail | lawPrison] or [bribe the officer].
