A bribe costs less than the bounty, and whether it works is a [dice check | partyDiceChecks] on the leader's [PSI | partyAttributes] against the officer's conscience.

- taken: the money is gone, and that officer looks the other way for a while
- refused: you keep the money, but offering it is [bribery], a crime of its own. You can try again
- an [incorruptible] officer can never be bought, and the offer still counts against you

lawJurisdictions.title: Whose Law Applies
lawJurisdictions.description:
Three codes of law rule the world, each keeping its own record. Which one you stand under depends on who holds the country.

- [common law]: most of the world
- [canon law]: the [Holy Vatican Empire | vaticanEmpire], with its own charges and its own blind spots
- [Horde law]: the [Goblin Horde | goblinHorde] punishes theft and little else

A [bounty | lawCrime] never crosses a border. The other record waits for you to come back.

Canon law is the harshest. A [Witch | partyClasses] or a [Gunmancer] in the party is marked on sight, and only a served sentence lifts that mark. An [Atheist] is fined, and casting [esoteric] or [forbidden] magic inside the Empire is heresy, witnessed or not.

In an empty world nobody is left to keep the law.

lawCriminalCareer.title: The Criminal's Trade
lawCriminalCareer.description:
Every crime teaches the trade behind it: shoplifting trains [Pickpocketing], burglary [Lockpicking], a bank job [Safecracking], fraud [Deception], and so on. Bigger jobs teach bigger lessons.

[Streetwise] training leaves less for the police to find, so the same deed costs a smaller [bounty | lawCrime].

A [Police Officer | partyClasses] in the party can sign off small charges as lawful acts every day, and what they sign never reaches the record. [Canon law | lawJurisdictions] accepts no badge.

A truly spectacular day of crime makes the front page of the [news | societyNews]. Beat [Eris | eris] in her own court and your bounty never grows again in that world.

economyWorkplaces.title: Buying a Workplace
economyWorkplaces.description:
Besides houses and shops you can buy a whole [business]: an indoor place where people work. Buy the one you stand in from the [Assets] screen, or any of them from the [Working places] tab of the [real estate board | econProperty].

The price depends on the staff it keeps, and never drops below [5000 euros]. Abandoned buildings and places already owned in your world cannot be bought.

The staff keep working and the business pays you a profit every [week]. In a thriving town it earns well; in a town on its knees it can lose money.

Owning it lets you [build | craftFurniture] there and makes its containers yours. Its people and its counters are not: [stealing | econStealing] there is still a crime. You can sell it back for a little less than you paid.

economyLandClaims.title: Claiming Land
economyLandClaims.description:
From the [Assets] screen you can [claim] the ground you stand on, for free. A claim lets you [build | craftFurniture] there and gives benched companions a place to wait.

The [world map | worldMapPage], settlements and roads can never be claimed.

Ground that already belongs to someone can still be taken, but that is squatting: you are warned first, and it costs a [trespassing | lawCrime] charge of [25 euros].

Give a claim up from the same screen, and whoever waited there comes home.

craftingTownFounding.title: Founding a Town
craftingTownFounding.description:
Three houses standing on one square of the world are enough to call it a town, whether you built them or found them there.

1. Open the [Town] tab of the [Build | craftFurniture] menu.
2. Give the place a name.
3. Sign the charter.

Your town belongs to the world: every party there finds it on the [world map | worldMapPage] and, on Earth, in the [travel book | travelOverview].

Newcomers drift in over the days and pay you rent. Every house you raise brings more of them. Collect what is owed from the [Assets] screen.

setupWorldCreation.title: Creating a World
setupWorldCreation.description:
New worlds are made from the [Worlds | worldsFolders] screen of the title menu. The form asks for:

- a [name] and a [seed]
- the [starting date | setupStartDate]
- the [starting level | setupStartLevel]
- the [alternate timeline | setupTimelines]: who lives there
- the [magic level | setupMagic]: how much magic there is
- the [reward multipliers | setupRewards]
- the [skill level limits | setupSkillLimits]

Everything is chosen [once]. No setting can be changed later: to play differently, make another world. A note under each row tells you what a choice means before you confirm.

setupTimelines.title: Alternate Timelines
setupTimelines.description:
The [alternate timeline] decides who lives in the world. It is picked once, and pairs with any [magic level | setupMagic].

[Normal]: history as it happened.

[World of chaos]: everything is drawn at random. Strange faces, strange shops, strange foes, and every level up teaches a [random skill | setupSkillLimits].

[Goblin mode]: everyone is a goblin, and the [Goblin Horde | goblinHorde] already rules most of Europe on the first day.

[Monster world]: no humans, elves or goblins. Towns are full of creatures, and some of them keep shop.

[Empty world]: everybody is gone. Shelves are never restocked, doors hang open, streetlights stay dark, and only mute monsters still roam.

[Zombie apocalypse | peopleZombies]: the walking dead fill the streets, living people are rare, and there is no talking your way out. Some shamble, some run.

[Death world]: an empty world with no monsters either. Nothing moves anywhere.

setupMagic.title: World Magic
setupMagic.description:
The [magic level] sets how much magic the world holds. It is picked once, and works with any [alternate timeline | setupTimelines].

[Normal]: everything exists.

[Severed magic]: magic never worked here. No spells, no magical classes or creatures, no enchanted gear, no [MP | combatAP], no brooms.

[Unbound magic]: magic won. Guns, machines and modern gadgets are never found, ordinary beasts give way to magical ones, and the ordinary classes cannot be picked.

Plain things, a rope, a sword, a loaf of bread, exist everywhere, and [Alchemistry | craftAlchemy] is studied under every level.

What the party is already [given] is never taken away. The level only decides what the world offers from then on.

setupStartDate.title: Starting Date
setupStartDate.description:
A world can begin any month from [January 2001] to [January 2013]. The years before your start are lived out first, so a later world already carries their history.

A later start is a harder world: monsters grow fiercer year after year, though a few countries stay gentle. In return, [loot | gearRarity] is richer. Pick a [starting level | setupStartLevel] to match, and remember the world keeps hardening as the clock runs.

[Story mode] is written for 2001. Any other year skips the tutorial.

A world that starts in [2013] begins after the impact of [21 December 2012]: there is no Earth, and the road leads to the [Omega Tower | omegaTower] instead. A world that reaches that day in play loses Earth the same way.

setupStartLevel.title: Starting Level
setupStartLevel.description:
Every character made in the world starts at this [level | progressLevels], anywhere from [1] to [99], already knowing the class skills that come with it.

A high starting level is what makes the later [starting dates | setupStartDate] survivable, and [loot | gearRarity] rises to match it.

[Story mode] always starts Em at level 1.

setupRewards.title: Reward Multipliers
setupRewards.description:
Three sliders on the world form decide how generously a [won fight | combatCorpses] pays: [experience | progressLevels], [money | econMoney] and [KP | progressKnowledge].

Slide left toward [nothing], right toward a feast, or leave them in the middle for a normal game.

Only fights are affected. [Quests | econQuests], [work | econWork] and shops pay as usual.

setupSkillLimits.title: Skill Level Limits
setupSkillLimits.description:
Two switches on the world form keep the rarest skills out of reach of beginners: one for [Esoteric] skills, one for [Forbidden] ones.

Both are on unless you turn them off. With a limit off, anyone can learn those skills from the [skill tree | progressAtlas], from [books | progressGrimoires] or from teachers, and in a [world of chaos | setupTimelines] a level up can hand them out freely.

A forbidden skill is esoteric too, so it still answers to the esoteric switch.

setupSandbox.title: Sandbox Mode
setupSandbox.description:
[Sandbox] on the title menu starts a free play party in the active world, as a powerful [Eris | eris] on the Disk of Discord.

A Sandbox page in the main menu does what you ask: start any battle, give any item, teleport anywhere, change time and weather, edit the world, and open the [Wishing Sanctum | gearWishOrb].

The rules bend too: skills, crafting at the [workbench | craftThinker] and the [forge | craftForge] and building cost nothing, crimes carry no bounty, and the [bestiary | combatBestiary] is already full.

The sandbox has its own save and is never autosaved.

needsRestWorth.title: What a Rest Gives Back
needsRestWorth.description:
A full night's rest brings HP, MP and AP all the way back, wears off every state and sets broken parts. A shorter rest gives its share, and short rests [add up] over time.

- [sleeping rough], with no bed, camp or bedding, is a poor rest that heals no wounds. A [Bedroll] in the pack or a bed nearby fixes that
- [waiting] heals no HP, but slowly restores AP and MP
- under [Blood and Oil | combatModes] a bed restores only MP and AP: the body keeps its wounds

A long sleep may slip into a [dream | worldDreams]. You can enter it or simply wake up.

The rest menu can also [save | savingGame] the game and [set your respawn point | partyDeath], except under Permadeath or Blood and Oil.

Sleep in battle counts too: dozing under the [Sleep | sleep] state rests you, and being [Wet | wet] washes you a little.

needsForage.title: Foraging for Hours
needsForage.description:
[Forage] in the rest menu spends the hours working instead of waiting. The party scatters over the ground and comes back with whatever the land gives: wild food and crafting materials.

More hands and training in [Foraging | progressSpecializations] bring back more, and every hour teaches a little [KP | progressKnowledge]. The work is tiring: sleep and hunger drain faster than when waiting.

A party that gets on well enjoys the [company | needsSocial]; one that does not drifts apart a little.

Foraging in a vehicle only turns up litter from under the seats.

needsCamp.title: Making Camp
needsCamp.description:
[Make a camp] from the [world map | worldMapPage] or the vehicle menu, and the [rest menu | needsRestWorth] opens as a camp.

A night at camp gives the usual rest and more: everyone freshens up a little on [hygiene | needsHygiene] and [company | needsSocial] around the fire.

If the party is hungry, somebody [cooks | craftCooking] from what is in the pack, smallest meals first. With nothing to cook, the camp tells you.

Waiting at camp is just as good as sleeping there. The camp is struck once you rest or leave the menu.

needsBladder.title: Bladder
needsBladder.description:
The [bladder] meter runs down with time, faster with every drink, especially alcohol and coffee. Asleep it runs slower, and a night's rest never ends in an accident.

When it runs low its chip warns you. A [WC], a shower, a bath or a [swim | worldMovement] sets things right for the whole party.

Wait too long and the member wets themselves on the spot, losing a good deal of hygiene and company. Creatures without a human mind do not care.

On the [world map | worldMapPage] or the open road the party simply pulls over by the roadside before it comes to that.

peopleHolidays.title: Holidays and Gatherings
peopleHolidays.description:
Every country keeps its own [public holidays], from Christmas and Easter to Eid, Diwali and national days. Lands ruled by a [hyperpower | peoplePolitics] keep its feasts too.

On a holiday offices and workshops close, while shops and the trades of a day off stay open.

Every holiday brings a [gathering] to town: a festival, a parade, a vigil or a protest. Rallies come before an [election | powersElections] and queues fill the polls on the day. The town pours into one square, and a notice tells you when it is under way.

The [Calendar | hypernetCalendar] on the [hyperdeck desktop | hypernetOS] lists holidays, elections, your [quest | econQuests] deadlines and your own appointments, with reminders.

gearWishOrb.title: The Wish-Granting Orb
gearWishOrb.description:
A [Wish-Granting Orb] can be bought for [10,000 euros] or [crafted | craftThinker]. Used from the menu, it restores the party fully and opens the [Wishing Sanctum].

The sanctum offers a spread of random wishes: an item, a fight, a sudden fortune, a [stock market | econStocks] boom, a body made whole again, and stranger things. Pick one and it comes true.

One orb, one wish. Leaving the sanctum without choosing wastes the orb.

A party with weak [PSI | partyAttributes] sees the wishes as riddles, or worse.

partyDiceChecks.title: Dice Checks
partyDiceChecks.description:
Many actions are settled by a [d20] thrown on screen: [stealing | econStealing], [trials | lawTrial], [surgery | healthSurgery], [cooking | craftCooking], [fusing spells | progressFusion], work shifts and chances the world offers you.

A strong [attribute | partyAttributes] adds to the roll, a weak one takes away. The total must reach the number shown.

- a [natural 20] always succeeds
- a [natural 1] always fails

When the world offers a check, a card shows what is being tested and what you need. You can [walk away] and nothing happens. The party leader rolls unless the check names someone else.

powersTravelJournal.title: The Travel Journal
powersTravelJournal.description:
Using a [Pocket Notebook], a [Travel Journal], a pen or a quill from the [backpack | gearBackpack] opens your [travel journal]: a notebook you write yourself.

Pick a page on the right and type on the left. Each page takes its name from its first line, and pages can be added or deleted.

The journal travels with your [save | savingGame], and on the desktop build its pages can be read outside the game too. Writing uses nothing up.
